findings.title: F1-F4 face-power sense taps land on RP2350 ADC pins, which are not fault-tolerant; an unpowered emulator exceeds their abs-max rating
findings.location: Emulator MCU / Solar and Sensor Emulation: U200 pins 40-43 (GPIO26_ADC0..GPIO29_ADC3) on nets EMU_F1_SENSE..EMU_F4_SENSE, pulled up by R314/R324/R334/R344 (4.7k) to F1_PWR..F4_PWR (FC AP22653 face switches U21 etc.)
findings.description: Each face-power sense tap is a 4.7k pull-up from the FC-switched face rail directly to an emulator GPIO. U200 runs from 3V3_EMU, which comes only from J701 USB through U202. F5 (GPIO24, pin 36) and FC +3V3 (GPIO22, pin 34) are on Digital IO (FT) pins. Those pins tolerate up to 3.63 V with IOVDD = 0 and draw very little current, so they are fine. F1-F4 are on GPIO26-29, which the RP2350 datasheet lists as 'Digital IO / Analogue', not FT, so the standard limit VPIN <= IOVDD + 0.5 V applies. If the FC turns on faces 1-4 while the emulator USB is unplugged, each pin sees about 3.3 V through 4.7k with IOVDD = 0. That exceeds abs max, and each pin injects about 0.5-0.6 mA through its ESD diode into the unpowered 3V3_EMU rail (about 2.2 mA total). The rail then partially powers U200, U201 and the D201 power LED through R211, with VREG_VIN well below its 2.7 V minimum. The sheet's design note says back-feed is limited to 'about 0.55 mA per line' into the ESD diode. That treats all six taps alike and misses that four of them sit on non-FT pins, where this is an abs-max violation and not the FT 'little current' case. The current is resistor-limited, so damage is unlikely. Partial powering of the emulator, and its undefined state before USB is applied, is a bench-reliability risk.
findings.evidence: Netlist: EMU_F1_SENSE = R314.2 + U200.40 (GPIO26_ADC0); EMU_F2_SENSE = R324.2 + U200.41; EMU_F3_SENSE = R334.2 + U200.42; EMU_F4_SENSE = R344.2 + U200.43. R314/R324/R334/R344 pin 1 = F1..F4_PWR (U21/... AP22653 outputs). 3V3_EMU is sourced only by U202.5 (VIN = VBUS_EMU from J701). EMU_F5_SENSE goes to U200.36 (GPIO24, FT) and EMU_FC3V3_SENSE to U200.34 (GPIO22, FT). RP2350 datasheet Table 1673: FT pins draw 'very little current whilst below 3.63 V and IOVDD is 0 V'. GPIO26-29 (Table 1674) are 'Digital IO / Analogue', not FT. 14.9 abs max: Voltage at IO (Standard) -0.5 to IOVDD+0.5 V. 6.1.5: 'Voltages greater than IOVDD will result in leakage currents through the ESD protection diodes.' Sheet note: 'limit back-feed into an unpowered emulator ESD diode to about 0.55 mA per line'.
findings.recommendation: Next rev: move the F1-F4 sense taps to FT GPIOs, or add a divider/clamp so the ADC pins never exceed 3V3_EMU + 0.5 V. Then route the four I2C pairs to ADC-free pins, or sense face power through the existing FT pins. This rev: add a bench procedure note to plug J701 (emulator USB) before the FC enables any face switch and to unplug it last, so IOVDD is present whenever F1-F4_PWR are on.
findings.reference: RP2350 datasheet RP-008373: 14.8.2.1 Table 1673 (pin types, FT definition), 14.8.2.2 Table 1674 (GPIO26-29 'Digital IO / Analogue'), 14.9 absolute maximum ratings (VPIN standard <= IOVDD+0.5 V), 6.1.5 ADC supply note

findings.title: FC powered with emulator unplugged: about 20 pull-ups feed 3V3_EMU through RP2350 ESD diodes, leaving U200 partly powered
findings.description: Each emulated face I2C line and each sense tap is pulled up to a rail the FC powers: F1_PWR to F5_PWR from the FC AP22653 load switches, and +3V3 for TOP and FC3V3_SENSE. The other end lands directly on a U200 GPIO, with no series element by design (hard rule 6). If the FC is on and the emulator USB (VBUS_EMU) is absent, these paths forward-bias the RP2350 I/O clamp diodes into 3V3_EMU, so the emulator partly powers up. The Phase-1 notes (sheet_emulator_mcu.md 6.3) already compute about 0.55 mA per line and a settled 3V3_EMU of about 2.4 V, with 'I/O state undefined'. The mitigation is only a bench rule printed on the sheet. The consequence is bounded and not damaging: Q701-Q703 gates have 4.7k pull-downs (R706/R708/R710), the CTL pins power up as inputs, and the current is under 1 mA per pin. The worst case is a spurious or partial boot of U200, which could briefly assert FC_RESET, USBBOOT or WDT_DISABLE. The path is real and not enforced by hardware. I list it for completeness. It is already owner-accepted and should not block the fab.

findings.title: L200 RP2350 VREG inductor is polarity-reversed relative to the RP2350 reference design and the flown FC (L3)
findings.location: emulator_mcu.kicad_sch L200 (Abracon AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T, LCSC C42411119); PCB L200 at (279.4, 90.75) F.Cu rot 0, footprint RP2350_60QFN_minimal:L_pol_2016
findings.description: The Abracon AOTA-B201610S3R3 is a polarity-marked inductor, made specifically so that RP2350 boards can fit it the right way round. The Raspberry Pi guide says regulator performance is 'massively improved' when the inductor is the right way round: a reversed winding couples its field into the regulator output capacitor and upsets the RP2350's VREG control loop. In both the official minimal design and the flown FC copy, footprint pad 1 (the dot) connects to the 1V1 side and pad 2 to VREG_LX. On L200 the symbol pins are swapped: pad 1 (dot) is on EMU_VREG_LX and pad 2 is on 1V1_EMU. The component description claims 'FC L3 parity', but the netlist shows the opposite polarity. The likely effect is 1V1_EMU regulation error or instability under load-current steps on the emulator MCU. It does not affect the FC copy.
findings.evidence: Netlist: L200 pin1=/Emulator MCU/EMU_VREG_LX, pin2=/Emulator MCU/1V1_EMU. FC heritage L3 pin1=+1V1, pin2=/RP2350.../VREG_LX. Official RPI-RP2350A-MINIMAL_R4-S1 (Minimal-KiCAD.zip): L1 pad1 '+1V1' at (-0.7,0) next to its silk dot at (-1.4,0.7), pad2 '/VREG_LX'. The two pads are symmetric, so the existing EMU_VREG_LX and 1V1_EMU tracks land on the same physical pad locations and the dot moves to the 1V1 side. findings.title: Bench Mode 2 feeds the battery-less FC from BQ25886 BAT, not SYS, so FC power is cut at charge termination, recharge deglitch and safety-timer expiry
findings.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: U511 pins 13/14 BAT (CHG_BAT) -> JP510 -> Dir_Chrg_In; U511 pins 15/16 SYS (CHG_SYS) loaded only by C513/C514/C517/C518/TP511
findings.description: Mode 2 (USB charger; JP510 fitted, PSU off, and by rule D11 no pack on J14) makes the BQ25886 the only source for Dir_Chrg_In, and its BAT pin is the output used. The datasheet's battery-less 'instant-on' path is SYS, not BAT. On BAT the charger runs a charge cycle into whatever is connected. (1) Below 4.4 V it supplies only 100 mA trickle, and below 6.0 V only ICHG/10 = 147 mA precharge, so an FC whose regulators start in that window and draw more can stall during start-up. (2) Once the FC load falls below ITERM (147 mA) for 250 ms, the charger terminates and turns the BATFET off. The 22 uF of CBAT plus the FC input capacitance then discharge in milliseconds, but recharge only restarts after a 250 ms deglitch below VREG - 200 mV, so the FC browns out repeatedly. This is the STAT-blinking no-battery cycle the sheet note calls 'expected'. (3) If the load stays above ITERM, the 12 h safety timer (24 h in DPM) expires and charging, and with it FC power, stops. The plug-in-and-go mode (D3) therefore cannot power the FC reliably. Mode 1 (PSU through the replica) is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Netlist: JP510 pin1=CHG_BAT (U511.13/14), pin2=Dir_Chrg_In; CHG_SYS members = C513, C514, C517, C518, TP511, U511.15/16 only. SLUSD88A: features list 'Instant-on works with no battery'; 8.3.6 NVDC: SYS regulated above VSYS_MIN 6.2 V even with no battery; 8.3.7.3 'After the charging cycle is completed, the BATFET turns off'; 8.3.7.1 'If no battery is connected, the STAT pin blinks as capacitance connected at BAT charges, discharges, then recharges'; IBAT_SHORT 100 mA below VBAT_SHORT 4.4 V; precharge = ICHG/10; tTERM_DGL 250 ms; tRECHG_DGL 250 ms; tSAFETY 12 h (8.3.7.5). Sheet text: 'Mode 2 USB charger: JP500 OPEN, JP510 fitted, bench PSU disconnected at J500'; D11 forbids a pack on J14 while J510 is live.
findings.recommendation: Fix this rev if Mode 2 is meant to power the FC: take the JP510 feed from CHG_SYS instead of CHG_BAT (cut the CHG_BAT trace at JP510.1 and wire TP511/CHG_SYS to JP510.1), and leave BAT with only C515. Otherwise, mark Mode 2 on the sheet and silkscreen as unsupported for powering the FC. Next rev: route SYS to the JP510 header in the schematic.
findings.reference: TI BQ25886 datasheet SLUSD88A, sections 1 (Features), 8.3.6 (power path / minimum system voltage), 8.3.7.1-8.3.7.3 (charging cycle, profile, termination), 8.3.7.5 (safety timer), Electrical Characteristics tTERM_DGL/tRECHG_DGL/tSAFETY

findings.title: Synthetic midpoint 2 x 1.0k 1% leaves no worst-case margin to the R5460N208AA over-charge threshold at the stated 8.4 V PSU limit
findings.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: R503/R504 (1.0k 1% 0805) -> MID_BENCH -> R501 -> U500 VC; J500 PSU window note '4.9 V <= V <= 8.4 V'
findings.description: In Mode 1 the top 'cell' seen by the R5460 is V(B+) x R503/(R503+R504). At the 8.4 V upper limit stated in the sheet note, with the resistors at opposite 1% extremes, the top cell is 8.4 x 1.01/2.00 = 4.242 V. That is above the R5460N208AA minimum over-charge detection threshold of 4.225 V (4.250 - 0.025 V at 25 C, and 4.220 V over -5 to 55 C). The LT3652 float of 8.38 V on Dir_Chrg_In when VSOLAR is injected gives about 4.232 V, which is also above the minimum. A COUT trip blocks charge current and leaves the FC fed through the Q501 body diode, so this is a test-validity nuisance (spurious OV trips) rather than damage.
findings.evidence: R503=R504=1.0k 1%; R5460 datasheet product table R5460x208AA VDET1=4.250 V; electrical characteristics VDET1 tolerance +/-0.025 V (25 C), +/-0.030 V (Ta -5 to 55 C); sheet note: 'Set the PSU to 8.4 V or less ... LT3652 float on this FC is 8.38 V, 120 mV below the over-charge trip' (this 120 mV figure uses the pack 8.50 V typical value and ignores divider mismatch and VDET1 tolerance).

Injection: Net-(D400-K) D400.1 -> via (239.46,148.40) -> In2 0.25 mm 14.4 mm -> JP400.1 (252.8,145.79); Net-(D401-K) In2 0.25 mm 16.4 mm -> JP401.1; Net-(D400-A)/(D401-A) F.Cu 0.25 mm ~6-7 mm. Charger: CHG_DVIN Q510.3/4 -> U511.23 bottleneck 0.187 mm with 3 x 0.20 vias; PMID Net-(C511-Pad1) U511.21/22 -> L510.2 0.25 mm incl. 7.2 mm In2; SW Net-(C512-Pad1) 0.25 mm 7.3 mm; CHG_BAT U511.13 -> JP510.1 0.25 mm In1 with 2 x 0.20 vias; VBUS_CHG and CHG_SYS bottleneck 0.25 mm. Pyro jumpers: VBUSP JP606.2 -> J30.1 bottleneck 0.25 mm (0.3 mm x 6.75 mm at x=189.625); INHIB_2 J10.3 stub 0.3 mm x 19.5 mm; B- J15.1 stub through one 0.46/0.20 via (214.83,142.955).
findings.description: The .kicad_pro patterns cover only named nets. The bench current-path nodes named by KiCad (FET common drain, Schottky anode/cathode, BQ25886 PMID and SW) match none of them; the brief's 'CHG_PMID' pattern never matched, because PMID is Net-(C511-Pad1). Even the named classes were not met: CHG_BAT, CHG_SYS, VBUS_CHG and VBAT_BENCH_N are in BenchPower (1.0 mm) but carry 0.25-0.30 mm segments. KiCad does not treat netclass track width as a DRC minimum, and FlatSat_V1.kicad_dru has no track_width rule, so DRC's '0 width items' did not test the brief's exit criterion 'no width below class'. Currents these nodes carry by design: up to 2 A (J500 window) through the Q500/Q501 loop and JP606/VBUSP; up to 1.2 A typical through D400/D401, with PTC F400/F401 holding up to 1.85 A (20 C) and tripping only at 3.7 A; up to 1.48 A input and 1.5 A ICHG in the BQ25886. A 0.25 mm trace on a 0.5 oz inner layer is roughly a 0.5-0.7 A conductor at 10 C rise (IPC-2152 internal charts), so the injection path cannot carry the PTC hold current, and the PTC no longer protects the copper. On the replica the series copper also changes what the replica measures. The Q500-Q501 common drain is about 45 mOhm (In1 is 15.2 um in the board stackup), plus about 12 mOhm of 0.3 mm F.Cu and vias on VBAT_BENCH_N. That sits inside the R5460 V- to VSS sense loop next to 2 x ~9 mOhm FET Rds(on). VDET3 = 0.2 V then trips near 2.5-3.5 A instead of the ~11 A the sheet note and battery_pack_v2 assume. A deploy or heater test drawing more than ~2.5 A would open DOUT and brown out the FC, and the cause would be the copper, not the pack behaviour.
findings.evidence: Widest-path search (new FlatSat copper, net by net): Q500 drain->Q501 drain 0.25; J500.3->Q500 source 0.30; D400.1->JP400.1 0.25; D401.1->JP401.1 0.25; Q510 S->U511 VBUS 0.187; U511 PMID->L510.2 0.25; U511 BAT->JP510.1 0.25; J510 VBUS->Q510 0.25; JP606.2->J30.1 0.25. Net-(Q500-D-Pad5) total copper resistance about 50 mOhm; Net-(D400-K) about 60 mOhm; Net-(D401-K) about 68 mOhm (0.5 oz inner). The .kicad_pro netclass_patterns list has no entry for Net-(Q500-D-Pad5), Net-(D40x-A/K), Net-(C511-Pad1), Net-(C512-Pad1) or CHG_DVIN. .kicad_dru has only clearance/annular/via rules, no track_width rule. The solar_power_injection sheet note gives F400/F401 Ihold 1.85 A and Itrip 3.70 A, and says 'the PTC does not protect the shunt either'. The battery_protection_replica note gives VDET3 0.200 V and 'about 11 A at 2 x 9 mOhm'.
findings.recommendation: Fix this rev (routing only, bench area plus attachment stubs, no heritage change). (1) Put local labels on the replica common drain, D400/D401 A/K, PMID, SW and CHG_DVIN, and add them to BenchPower. (2) Add .kicad_dru rules (constraint track_width (min 1.0mm)) for BenchPower/FCPower outside the attachment pads, with a narrower per-pad neck allowed only at the heritage connector pads. Add a via-count check or two vias per layer change. (3) Re-route Q500/Q501 common drain as a short F.Cu pour between the two SOIC-8 drain rows (place the FETs drain-to-drain). Re-route D40x->JP40x, the BQ25886 PMID-L510-SW loop (per the BQ25886 layout guidelines: short, wide SW/inductor path) and VBUS/CHG_DVIN at 1.0 mm or more on outer layers. Widen JP606/VBUSP and the J15.1 B- stub as far as the pad allows. Then re-check the R5460 trip current against the replica intent.
findings.reference: Brief 00_pm_brief.md L5 (BenchPower 1.0 mm, FC-net new tracks 1.0 mm min, two vias per layer change; bench currents ~3 A shunt paths, 1.5 A charger, 1.2 A injection) and §9 exit criterion 'no width below class'; IPC-2152; R5460N208AA datasheet VDET3 excess-discharge detection; Littelfuse 2920L datasheet Ihold/Itrip; TI BQ25886 SLUSD88A §11 Layout Guidelines

findings.title: Mode 2 powers the FC from BQ25886 BAT with no cell: precharge current limit, termination cycling and safety timer can drop the FC
findings.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: U511 BAT (pins 13/14, CHG_BAT) -> JP510 -> Dir_Chrg_In; CHG_SYS (U511.15/16, C513/C514/C517/C518, TP511) has no load; ICHGSET R515 5.62k
findings.description: In Mode 2 (JP510 fitted, no pack, since J14 must not carry a real pack while emulation is fitted), the FC load hangs on the charger's BAT pin. BAT is a charge-controlled port, not a regulated supply: below VBAT_LOWV the charger limits current to precharge ICHG/10 (about 150 mA with R515 5.62k). Above it, CC/CV runs with termination at ICHG/10, recharge cycling, and STAT blinking with no battery (sheet doc quotes §8.3.7.1). The safety timer also applies (§8.3.7.5: fixed 2 h precharge timer, fast-charge timer counted at half rate in input-current regulation; charging stops on expiry). With a continuous FC load above the termination current, charge never terminates, so the fast-charge timer runs out during a long soak and the BAT output stops sourcing. With a load below it, the FC sees termination/recharge sawtooth. A boot draw above ~150 mA while BAT is below VBAT_LOWV can also stall start-up. The datasheet's narrow-VDC SYS output is the path meant to power a system with no or dead battery, and here it is left unloaded. The sheet docs do not analyse Mode 2 with the FC as the only BAT load.
findings.evidence: Netlist: CHG_BAT = C515.1, JP510.1, TP512.1, U511.13, U511.14; CHG_SYS = C513/C514/C517/C518, TP511, U511.15/16 (no load). ICHG = 5.62k / 3810 ohm/A = 1.47 A, precharge/termination ICHG/10 = 0.15 A (sheet doc §9.2.2.5). BQ25886 §8.3.7.5: precharge 2 h fixed; timer suspended only in fault/supplement; reset only on CE toggle or recharge. Sheet note 'Mode 2 USB charger: JP500 OPEN, JP510 fitted, bench PSU disconnected'.
findings.recommendation: Next rev: move JP510 pin 1 to CHG_SYS (narrow-VDC system output) or add a second jumper SYS->Dir_Chrg_In, keeping the same 'never with J500 PSU' rule. This rev: verify at bring-up with the FC at its worst-case boot and steady load. If Mode 2 misbehaves, use a wire from TP511 (CHG_SYS) to TP500 (Dir_Chrg_In) instead of the JP510 shunt, and limit Mode 2 soaks to shorter than the fast-charge timer.
findings.reference: TI BQ25886 datasheet SLUSD88A §8.3.6.1 Narrow VDC architecture, §8.3.7.1 STAT (no-battery blinking), §8.3.7.5 Charging Safety Timer, §9.2.2.5 ICHGSET

findings.title: VSOLAR injection has no over-voltage clamp in front of the FC's INA219 U8 (26 V abs max); protection relies only on bench-PSU setting/OVP
findings.location: solar_power_injection.kicad_sch J400/J401 -> F400/F401 (33 V PTC) -> D400/D401 -> JP400/JP401 -> VSOLAR (FC: INA219 U8 IN+, LT3652 IC6 VIN)
findings.description: The injection path has reverse-polarity (Schottky) and overcurrent (PTC) protection but nothing that limits voltage. Bench PSUs commonly reach 30-32 V, and the documented hard maximum (24 V) leaves 2 V to the INA219 U8 26 V absolute maximum on the frozen FC copy. A mis-set knob, a PSU in series/tracking mode, or a supply turned up past 26 V destroys U8 (and above 32 V the LT3652), with no element on the board that responds. This is a known, documented choice (the sheet says 'No TVS fitted... bench PSU OVP is the primary defense'). It is listed because it is the one bench input where a single operator error damages FC-copy silicon.
findings.evidence: Sheet text: 'HARD MAXIMUM 24 V (F400/F401 are 33 V Vmax)'; 'INA219 U8 (0x41) IN+ absolute maximum on VSOLAR is 26 V'; 'LT3652 IC6 operating maximum input is 32 V'; 'No TVS fitted on VSOLAR_BENCH_A/B'. Netlist: VSOLAR_BENCH_A J400.1 -> F400 -> D400 -> JP400 -> VSOLAR with no shunt element.
findings.recommendation: Next rev: add an over-voltage cut-off on each channel (e.g. an OV-protection load switch or a Zener-gated PMOS that opens above ~22 V) downstream of the PTC. A plain TVS clamps too high to protect a 26 V part. This rev: require a PSU with OVP set at 22 V or below in the bench procedure, and put '24 V MAX' on the silkscreen next to J400/J401 if it is not already there.
findings.reference: TI INA219 datasheet §7.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings (IN+/IN- 26 V); ADI LT3652 datasheet Absolute Maximum Ratings; sheet note on solar_power_injection.kicad_sch

findings.title: J500 reversed leads reverse-bias the R5460 replica through R500 330 ohm (no reverse-polarity element on J500)
findings.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch J500 pin1 Dir_Chrg_In / pin3 VBAT_BENCH_N; U500 VDD via R500 (330, 0603) from Dir_Chrg_In, VSS = VBAT_BENCH_N
findings.description: With PSU + on pin 3 and - on pin 1, U500 VSS sits up to ~8.4 V above VDD. Q500 conducts through its body diode, but Q501 (COUT low, unpowered) blocks drain-to-source, so the FC copy sees only milliamps: through R505 100k and through R502 1k via the U500 V- pin. The FC is therefore protected. The replica is not: the R5460 VSS-to-VDD substrate/ESD path is fed through R500 alone, about (8.4-0.7)/330 = 23 mA and about 0.18 W in a 0.1 W 0603, beyond the IC's VDD-VSS -0.3 V absolute minimum. That is likely to damage U500 or R500, so a later Mode-1 run would test a broken protection replica. The JP500 divider adds a harmless ~4 mA.
findings.evidence: Netlist: R500.1 Dir_Chrg_In, R500.2 U500.5 VDD; U500.6 VSS = VBAT_BENCH_N = J500.3; Q500 S = VBAT_BENCH_N, Q501 S = B-, common drain Net-(Q500-D-Pad5); R505 100k VBAT_BENCH_N-B-; R502 1k U500.3-B-.
findings.recommendation: Next rev: add a series Schottky or a PMOS ideal-diode on J500 pin 1, or a reverse diode across pins 1-3 behind a PTC. This rev: polarity silk (already in L8), keyed or colour-coded leads, and a bring-up check of TP503/TP504 gate drive after any lead mix-up.
findings.reference: Ricoh R5460N datasheet Absolute Maximum Ratings (VDD-VSS); battery_protection_replica sheet notes

findings.title: Battery-FET common-drain link routed as 0.25 mm / 15 um In1 trace: adds about 42 mOhm to the R5460N over-current sense path
findings.description: Q500 and Q501 are series back-to-back MOSFETs; their shared drain net Net-(Q500-D-Pad5) carries the full battery current. It is not in any netclass pattern, so it was routed Default: F.Cu 0.25 mm tie, one 0.46/0.20 via at each end, and a 6.9 mm In1.Cu run at 0.25 mm. In1 is the 15.2 um (0.5 oz) layer in the stackup, about 1.13 mOhm/sq, so 27.6 sq is about 31 mOhm; F.Cu stubs add about 8 mOhm and the two vias about 3 mOhm, so about 42 mOhm in total. The schematic note says excess-discharge VDET3 = 0.200 V across Q500+Q501 (about 11 A at 2 x 9 mOhm). U500 senses V- (via R502 from B-) against VSS (VBAT_BENCH_N), so the sensed drop includes this link. With about 60 mOhm total the 12 ms excess-discharge trip falls to about 3.3 A instead of about 11 A. Brief L5 states bench currents up to about 3 A and calls for 1.0 mm tracks and two vias per layer change on the battery-path nets. The 1.5 A charger current also flows through this link when charging via the FETs; heating there is about 70 mW. This is not a short or DRC error (DRC passes), but the replica protection no longer behaves like the flown pack's.
findings.recommendation: Add this net to BenchPower and tie Q500 pads 5-8 to Q501 pads 5-8 with at least 1.5 mm copper on F.Cu or B.Cu plus two or more 0.8/0.4 vias, or a surface pour, so the link is under 5 mOhm. For the current board a bodge (heavy wire or solder bridge from Q500 drain pads to Q501 drain pads) restores the intended threshold. If bench loads (heater, burn-wire dummy loads) stay under 2.5 A, this is next-rev; if loads over 3 A are planned, treat as fix-this-rev.
findings.reference: Battery replica sheet note (VDET3 0.200 V); PM brief L5 (BenchPower 1.0 mm, two vias per layer change, bench currents about 3 A); Nisshinbo R5460 datasheet (excess-discharge detect measured V- to VSS); IPC-2152 sheet-resistance basis

findings.title: BQ25886 power path and VSOLAR injection chain routed at default 0.25 mm contrary to brief L5
findings.location: Nets CHG_BAT, CHG_DVIN, Net-(C512-Pad1) (SW), Net-(C511-Pad1) (PMID), Net-(D400-A), Net-(D400-K), Net-(D401-K); U511 / L510 / Q510 / F400 / D400 area
findings.description: Several series power nets did not get the BenchPower/FCPower width. CHG_BAT is listed in the BenchPower patterns but is still routed 0.25 mm on F.Cu (3.4 mm) and In1 (14.4 mm, 15 um copper) with single 0.46/0.20 vias; R515 = 5.62k sets ICHG about 1.475 A, so the path is roughly 75 mOhm, about 0.11 V and 0.17 W at full charge current, and U511 regulates at the BAT pin before this drop. The boost SW node (L510.1 to U511.17/18) is 7.3 mm of 0.25 mm trace and PMID (L510.2) is 0.25 mm F.Cu plus In2. findings.title: L200 (RP2350 VREG inductor) polarity is reversed: the dot pad is on VREG_LX, but the Raspberry Pi reference and the flown L3 put it on DVDD
findings.location: emulator_mcu sheet / L200 (F.Cu 279.4,90.75 mm), nets /Emulator MCU/EMU_VREG_LX and 1V1_EMU
findings.description: L200 is the polarity-marked Abracon AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T (LCSC C42411119) on footprint RP2350_60QFN_minimal:L_pol_2016, where pad 1 carries the polarity dot (F.Fab circle at pad 1). In the Raspberry Pi minimal design L1, pin 1 is +1V1 and pin 2 is VREG_LX. The flown FC copy L3 on this board is the same. On FlatSat L200, pin 1 (the dot) is EMU_VREG_LX and pin 2 is 1V1_EMU, so the inductor is the 'wrong way round'. Raspberry Pi found that this makes the inductor's stray field couple into COUT and upset the RP2350 regulator control loop. The L200 field description says 'FC L3 parity', but the pins do not match L3.
findings.evidence: Netlist pins: L200.1 = /Emulator MCU/EMU_VREG_LX and L200.2 = /Emulator MCU/1V1_EMU. L3.1 = +1V1 and L3.2 = VREG_LX. Reference RPI-RP2350A-MINIMAL_R4-S1: L1.1 = +1V1, L1.2 = /VREG_LX. PCB pads: L200 pad 1 at 278.7,90.75 = LX, pad 2 at 280.1,90.75 = 1V1. The F.Fab polarity circle sits at the pad-1 offset (-0.7,0) on both L200 and L1.
findings.recommendation: Fix this rev, because it is cheap. In emulator_mcu.kicad_sch swap the L200 pin nets so that pin 1 is 1V1_EMU and pin 2 is EMU_VREG_LX, as on L3 and the reference. Then rotate L200 by 180 degrees: the LX pad stays on the west side next to U200 pin 48, so the existing routing geometry is kept.
findings.reference: Raspberry Pi 'Hardware design with RP2350' §2.1 (pp.6-8, inductor orientation; 'if you choose not to use our example, then you do so at your own risk'); RP2350 datasheet §6.3.8 Fig.26 (orientation indicator); RPI-RP2350A-MINIMAL_R4-S1 KiCad reference

findings.title: BQ25886 SYS hot loop is long and goes through vias: SYS caps are 4.5 mm away on the other side of two 0.2 mm vias, with no GND vias at any charger cap or the EP
findings.location: battery_protection_replica sheet / U511 (F.Cu 277.0,152.2), C513/C514/C517/C518 (CHG_SYS), C515 (CHG_BAT), C511 (PMID), L510
findings.description:
TI's layout priority 1 is to put the SYS output cap (the boost hot loop SW -> HS FET -> SYS -> CSYS -> PGND -> LS FET) as close as possible to the SYS and GND pins. The board instead reaches CSYS through two 0.2 mm vias and In2, then returns through 7.6 mm of F.Cu pour and the In1 plane (or about 20 mm of F.Cu) to PGND pins 19/20. There is no small high-frequency SYS cap at the pins. The extra loop inductance (likely several nH) raises the SW-node overshoot. SW runs at about 8.4-9 V, and the SW absolute maximum is 13 V. The datasheet notes that switching spikes must not exceed the SW absolute maximum and that a tight layout minimises them. The other datasheet layout points are also missed:
- The EP has no thermal vias (item 6: 'critical').
- SW and PMID, which carry the full 1.48 A input current, are 0.25 mm traces; PMID runs 5.5 mm on In2 (0.5 oz).
- CHG_BAT (up to about 0.9 A) runs 14.4 mm as a 0.25 mm trace on In1, the GND plane layer, under U511.
- None of the 22 uF charger caps has a GND via within 3 mm.

verdicts.evidence_checked: netlist.xml: VSOLAR_BENCH_A = J400.1, F400.1, TP400.1; Net-(D400-A) = F400.2, D400.2(A); Net-(D400-K) = D400.1(K), JP400.1; VSOLAR = J1/J2/J6/J9/J11/J13 pins 1-2, JP400.2, JP401.2, R108.1, TP401.1, U8.1 (IN+). Channel B is the same (F401/D401/JP401). V_SOLAR_SENSE = R108.2, U8.2 (IN-), IC6.1 VIN, IC6.3 SHDN, C40, R65. No TVS, Zener, crowbar or OV switch on any of these nets; the only parts are series parts. Sheet text in solar_power_injection.kicad_sch confirms 'HARD MAXIMUM 24 V', 'INA219 U8 ... IN+ absolute maximum on VSOLAR is 26 V', 'LT3652 IC6 operating maximum input is 32 V' and 'No TVS fitted ... bench PSU OVP is the primary defense'. docs/flatsat/2026-09-14_phase1_schematic/00_pm_brief.md:177 (a TVS is optional, standoff <=22 V if fitted, PSU OVP primary) and :254 (R9 'No TVS on VSOLAR_BENCH_A/B ... Accepted. Bench PSU OVP is the primary protection'). 01_brief_critique.md section 6 cites INA219 SBOS448 section 7.1: IN+/IN- common-mode -0.3 to 26 V, 'In no event should more than 26 V be applied'; LT3652: VIN 4.95-32 V operating, 40 V absolute maximum. The TI PDF I fetched would not convert to text on this machine, so these figures come from the repo critique and agree with my own reading of the datasheets. PCB silkscreen (gr_text) near the terminals reads only 'VSOLAR A' at (253.05,152.43) and 'VSOLAR B' at (226.2,162.82). No board text gives a voltage maximum, so the silkscreen part of the recommendation is not already done. Side note, outside this finding: heritage C40 (LT3652 VIN bypass on V_SOLAR_SENSE) is 10uF 10V X5R 0603. Rev2 BOM has LCSC C19702. Its rating is below the 12-24 V bench window. It is frozen Rev2 heritage and identical to flight.
verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the evidence. Each bench VSOLAR channel goes J40x -> PTC -> Schottky -> shunt jumper -> VSOLAR, which lands directly on INA219 U8 IN+ and, through the 2 mOhm R108, on LT3652 IC6 VIN. Nothing in that path limits voltage. With about 0.3-0.5 V dropped across the PTC and Schottky, a bench supply set above about 26.5 V exceeds the U8 absolute maximum. Common 0-30 V or 0-32 V lab supplies can reach that with one wrong turn of the knob. This works against the PM goal that the board 'cannot damage the FC copy'. It is not a defect against the spec, though. The PM brief explicitly accepted it as ruling R9 (no TVS, PSU OVP is primary protection), and the sheet documents it, so it is an accepted bench-practice risk. It cannot cause a failure under the documented 12-18 V nominal / 24 V maximum procedure. Minor severity and next-rev disposition are right, and no fix is needed this rev. Two corrections to the finding. (1) The cheap this-rev mitigation the reviewer suggests is real: there is no '24 V MAX' silkscreen. The board shows only 'VSOLAR A' and 'VSOLAR B', and the limit lives only in the schematic text. (2) 'A plain TVS clamps too high' is only partly right. Against a current-limited bench supply, a 20-22 V standoff SMA TVS conducts near its breakdown voltage (about 22-27 V), well below its rated Ipp clamp voltage. The margin to 26 V is still too thin, and the TVS would overheat unless the PSU current limit is low. An OV cut-off switch (Zener-gated PMOS or an OVP load-switch IC) after the PTC is still the better next-rev fix. Not heritage-validated: the injection path is new (refdes 400 series).
verdicts.corrected_description: Bench VSOLAR injection (J400/J401 -> F400/F401 -> D400/D401 -> JP400/JP401 -> VSOLAR) has reverse-polarity and overcurrent protection but no over-voltage limiting. A bench supply set above about 26.5 V puts more than the 26 V absolute maximum on FC-copy INA219 U8 IN+, and above 32 V it exceeds the LT3652 IC6 operating range. This is an owner-accepted choice (PM brief R9: no TVS, PSU OVP is primary protection), documented only in the schematic text. No silkscreen voltage limit is printed next to the terminals. Disposition: next-rev, add an OV cut-off switch after the PTC. This rev: the bench procedure should require PSU OVP at 24 V or below, and a '24 V MAX' label should go near J400/J401 (silkscreen next rev, or a sticker on the built boards).

verdicts.evidence_checked: Netlist: R503 and R504 are both '1.0k 1%' 0805 (C17513). JP500-A connects to R503.1, R503.2 and R504.1 sit on MID_BENCH (with J500.2, R501.2 and TP505), and R504.2 sits on VBAT_BENCH_N (U500.6 VSS). R501 330 ohm runs from MID_BENCH to U500.4 VC, and R500 330 ohm runs from Dir_Chrg_In to U500.5 VDD. Sheet notes give 'BENCH PSU WINDOW: 4.9 V <= V(B+ - B-) <= 8.4 V' and 'Set the PSU to 8.4 V or less: the LT3652 float on this FC is 8.38 V, 120 mV below the over-charge trip.' R5460 datasheet EA-165-250616: the product code table lists R5460x208AA with VDET1 = 4.250 V. Electrical Characteristics p.6 give VDET1U and VDET1L at VDET1 +/-0.025 V (25 C, R1 = R2 = 330 ohm) and +/-0.030 V over Ta -5 to 55 C. Technical Notes p.17 say that a larger R1/R2 shifts detection higher because of conduction current, but IDD is 4 uA typ / 8 uA max, so the extra 500 ohm of divider Thevenin resistance adds only a few mV. verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the numbers. The per-cell fraction is R503/(R503+R504), and with the resistors at opposite 1% limits it reaches 1.01/2.00 = 0.505. At 8.40 V that puts 4.242 V on one cell, above the 4.225 V minimum VDET1 at 25 C. Worst case, the pack can trip at 4.225/0.505 = 8.366 V, which is below the 8.378 V LT3652 float. The sheet's '120 mV below the trip' figure therefore holds only with typical VDET1 and a perfect divider. With minimum VDET1 and a perfect divider the margin is 70 mV, and in the full worst case it is negative. The VC series-resistance effect is at the mV level and does not change this. Impact is as the reviewer says, and the risk is only statistical: a trip needs both resistors near opposite tolerance limits and U500 near its low threshold, while same-reel 1% parts usually match to about 0.2%. With a 0.2% mismatch the cell sees 4.208 V and nothing trips. A COUT trip only switches off Q501, so FC load current keeps flowing through the Q501 body diode with about a 0.7 V drop. The sheet already tells the operator that a COUT opening is expected pack behaviour, so no hardware is damaged. A real pack with 1% cell imbalance would trip the same way. This is a margin and documentation error in a new FlatSat circuit, not heritage. Severity stays minor at most (next rev: tighter or matched R503/R504; this rev: lower the PSU limit in the note to about 8.3 V).

Worst case, the replica can trip COUT at 8.366 V, below the FC LT3652 float of 8.378 V. The sheet's '120 mV margin' claim uses typical VDET1 and an ideal divider; the worst-case margin is negative. The consequence is a possible spurious COUT trip: charge is blocked and the FC is fed through the Q501 body diode with about a 0.7 V drop. This is a test-validity nuisance with low practical probability, not a damage risk.

The converter keeps running to power the system.' §8.3.7.1 and Table 5: pre-charge and termination current are ICHG/10, recharge is at VREG - 200 mV, and with no battery 'STAT blinks as capacitance connected at BAT charges, discharges, then recharges'. The safety timer is 12 h. Electrical table: IBAT_SHORT = 100 mA below VBAT_SHORT 4.4 V; VBAT_LOWV = 6.0 V; ITERM is 143-159 mA at 25 C and 120-180 mA over 0-85 C for ICHG 1.5 A. Timing table: tTERM_DGL 250 ms, tRECHG_DGL 250 ms, tSAFETY 10.8-13.2 h. §8.3.7.5: the timer counts at half rate in DPM, and the 2 h pre-charge timer runs while VBAT < VBAT_LOWV. Table 6 lists timer fault as charge suspend (STAT blinking). R515 5.62k gives ICHG = 1.475 A, so ITERM and IPRECHG are about 147 mA.
verdicts.reasoning: Every datasheet mechanism the reviewer cites reproduces, and the impact is understated. Mode 2 always has no battery (D11), so BAT, a charge-controlled port, is the FC's only supply. (1) FC load at 8.4 V below ITERM (about 120-180 mA): the charger terminates after the 250 ms deglitch and turns the BATFET off (§8.3.7.3), and nothing then sources BAT. This is likely for an idle RP2350 FC, since 3.3 V rail loads of order 100 mA reflect to roughly 50-80 mA at 8.4 V. The about 130-240 uF of FC input capacitance then discharges at hundreds of V/s, so the FC reaches regulator UVLO within milliseconds, long before the 250 ms recharge deglitch ends. The result is a brownout and reboot cycle, not the benign sawtooth the reviewer describes. On restart BAT passes through the 100 mA trickle and 147 mA pre-charge limits below 4.4 V and 6.0 V, so a constant-power FC load can stall start-up. (2) FC load above ITERM: termination never occurs, and the 12 h safety timer (10.8-13.2 h, or 24 h in DPM) expires and suspends charging, ending a long soak. The datasheet's no-battery 'instant-on' path is SYS, which is left unloaded here. debug_board_v1 is no heritage: it was never assembled, and it was meant to charge a pack. No hardware is damaged, Mode 1 (PSU through the replica) is unaffected, and a bench rework exists without a respin (JP510 open, wire TP511 CHG_SYS to TP500 Dir_Chrg_In, keeping the no-PSU rule). Even so, the USB 'plug in and go' mode probably cannot keep a running FC powered, so I raise the severity from minor to major. Disposition: this rev, document the rework and bring-up check; next rev, move JP510.1 to CHG_SYS. The FC idle current at 8.4 V is not documented in the repo, but whichever side of ITERM it falls on, one of the two failure modes applies.

Restarts pass through the 100 mA trickle and 147 mA pre-charge limits. If the FC draws more than ITERM, charge never terminates and the 12 h safety timer (24 h in DPM) eventually suspends BAT. The official RPI-RP2350A-MINIMAL_R4-S1 PCB (scratchpad/ds/mindes) has L1 pad1=+1V1. So the net-level difference is real. I then compared geometry in each chip's local frame. Reference L1 sits above the pin row at local (1.3,-7.2)=+1V1/dot and (2.7,-7.2)=LX, with C7 directly below it (+1V1 left, GND right). FC L3 matches at (1.49,-7.45)=+1V1 and (2.89,-7.45)=LX. FlatSat L200 sits east of U200 at local (5.56,-4.11)=LX/dot and (6.95,-4.11)=1V1, with C_OUT C217 below it (GND left at 5.14, 1V1 right at 6.17). RP2350 datasheet 6.3.8.2/6.3.8.3 and Fig. 26/28 (rendered pp.411/413): the coil is a planar spiral (vertical field axis); current enters + and leaves at the dot; Fig. 26 puts the dot on V_OUT for that specific layout.
verdicts.reasoning: The emulator's regulator layout mirrors Fig. 26 left to right. The LX pad is nearest the chip on the left and V_OUT on the right. C_OUT has GND on the left and V_OUT on the right. The LX-L-C_OUT-PGND loop circulates clockwise seen from the top, against counter-clockwise in Fig. 26 and on the FC. The datasheet's concern is the sign of the coupling between the inductor's vertical leakage field and that loop. The part keeps rot 0 with the dot on the left, and current now runs dot to non-dot, so the coil's field is reversed. Reversed field through a reversed loop gives the same coupling sign as the reference. The as-built dot-on-LX is therefore the mirror-consistent choice. The reviewer compared net assignments without the geometry. The proposed fix (rotate 180 and swap pins) keeps the coil sense of the reference while the loop stays mirrored, so it would flip the coupling sign: it creates the 'wrong way round' condition rather than curing it. verdicts.reasoning: In Mode 2 the FC is the only load on BQ25886 BAT, so the charger treats FC current as charge current. Once BAT reaches VREG (it holds only about 22 uF plus the FC input caps, so this is almost immediate) and the FC draw stays under about 147 mA for 250 ms, the charge terminates and the BATFET opens. BAT then sags at roughly 1-2 V/ms under FC load, and recharge cannot restart for at least 250 ms. The FC therefore power-cycles, which is the 'expected' STAT blinking with the FC as the victim. If the FC draws more than ITERM, it is instead cut off when the 12-24 h safety timer expires. Start-up is limited to 100 mA below 4.4 V and 147 mA below 6.0 V. Powering the FC from SYS (instant-on, held at or above VSYS_MIN or VBAT+50 mV while the converter runs) avoids all three. Severity stays major: one of the three documented bench modes cannot reliably power the FC copy. There is no damage path, and Mode 1 is unaffected. Low-cost fix: feed JP510.1 from CHG_SYS (TP511 is on that net), or mark Mode 2 as not for powering the FC.

verdicts.evidence_checked: Netlist: EMU_F1_SENSE=R314.2+U200.40 (GPIO26_ADC0), EMU_F2_SENSE=R324.2+U200.41, EMU_F3_SENSE=R334.2+U200.42, EMU_F4_SENSE=R344.2+U200.43. R3x4 pin1=F1..F4_PWR, the AP22653 outputs (U21/U22/U24/U23, input +3V3). EMU_F5_SENSE goes to U200.36 (GPIO24) and EMU_FC3V3_SENSE to U200.34 (GPIO22). 3V3_EMU is sourced only by U202.5 (AP2112K, VIN=EN=VBUS_EMU from J701). The rail's only DC load is R211 1k + D201. RP2350 datasheet: Table 1673 (FT definition), Table 1674 (GPIO0-25 'Digital IO (FT)'; GPIO26_ADC0-GPIO29_ADC3 'Digital IO / Analogue'), Table 1680 abs max (VPIN -0.5 to IOVDD+0.5 V; VPIN_FT up to 3.63 V at IOVDD=0), and the ADC section ('Voltages greater than IOVDD will result in leakage currents through the ESD protection diodes'). Bench rule printed on emulator_mcu.kicad_sch.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly. With the FC enabling faces 1-4 and the emulator USB absent, the four ADC pins sit at about 3.3 V through 4.7k while IOVDD/ADC_AVDD is near 0-2.2 V. That exceeds VPIN max = IOVDD+0.5 V, and these are the only real back-feed paths into 3V3_EMU, since the other sense and I2C pins are FT. Injection is resistor-limited: at most 0.55 mA per pin with the rail at 0, and about 0.1 mA per pin once the rail settles near 2.2 V against the LED load. Damage is therefore unlikely. The effect is partial powering of U200, U201 and D201 with VREG_VIN below its 2.7 V minimum. The printed sheet note does treat all lines as alike, as the finding says. Minor, next rev. The this-rev mitigation (USB before FC face enables) is already printed on the sheet and should go into the bring-up checklist.

verdicts.evidence_checked: Netlist: J500.1=Dir_Chrg_In, J500.2=MID_BENCH, J500.3=VBAT_BENCH_N, with no series or shunt polarity element. R500 330 ohm 0603 (C23138, 0.1 W class) from Dir_Chrg_In to U500.5 VDD. U500.6 VSS=VBAT_BENCH_N. C500 VDD-VSS. Q500 (IRF7458) S=VBAT_BENCH_N; Q501 S=B-; common drain Net-(Q500-D-Pad5). R505 100k VBAT_BENCH_N-B-. R502 1k U500.3 V- to B-. R504/R503 1k/1k divider via JP500 (default FIT). R501 330 ohm from MID_BENCH to VC. B- reaches GND only through JP607/J15/J19. R5460 datasheet (EA-165) abs max: VDD -0.3 to 12 V (VSS=0); VC VSS-0.3 to VDD+0.3.
verdicts.reasoning: With + on pin 3 and - on pin 1, the path PSU+ to VSS, through U500's VSS-VDD junction and R500, to PSU- carries about (8.4-0.7)/330 = 23 mA, about 0.18 W in a 0.1 W 0603 (0.13 W at 7.4 V, 0.05 W at 4.9 V). That violates U500's VDD-VSS -0.3 V minimum; with no internal junction the violation would be the full -8.4 V. The VC pin adds about 4 mA through R501 from the JP500 divider node, and the divider itself about 3-4 mA. Q500's body diode conducts but Q501's body diode blocks drain to B-, so the FC copy sees only milliamps via R505/R502, provided Q501 stays off. That last point rests on COUT being low while U500 is reverse-supplied, which the datasheet does not specify. It is a small residual risk the finding states as fact. 'Likely damage' is overstated: R500 sits at 1.3-1.8 times its rating and U500 takes about 25 mA of substrate current. Degradation is plausible, not certain. This is a human-error scenario with polarity silk already planned (L8). Minor, next rev, with a bring-up check after any lead mix-up as recommended.

verdicts.evidence_checked: Dumped the current FlatSat_V1.kicad_pcb with pcbnew (vchg/board.pkl) and rasterised the filled F.Cu/In1/In2/B.Cu copper around U511 (vchg/chg_*.png, u511_zoom.png). Ran a geodesic BFS over F.Cu GND copper (vchg/geo.py). Read BQ25886 SLUSD88A text (§7.1 abs max, pin table, §11.1). U511 EP (pad 25, 2.7x2.7 at 277.0,152.2) has 0 vias. It reaches pins 4/5/20 only through F.Cu zone slivers. Within 12 mm of U511 there are only 4 GND vias: 278.0,149.523 (2.86 mm), 275.489,156.887 (4.92 mm), 278.425,159.45 and 288.4,151.55. CHG_SYS path: pins 15/16 -> 0.25 mm F.Cu -> via 279.663,152.2 (0.46/0.20) -> In2 1.5 mm, about 5.7 mm -> via 281.462,154.95 -> C513.1. Pin-to-C513.1 is 4.51 mm centre to centre, the same figure as audit_charger_bq25886.md. No other cap is on CHG_SYS (netlist: C513/C514/C517/C518/TP511). C514/C518 reach the C513/C517 column only through a 0.25 mm x 3.26 mm F.Cu link at y=158.277. F.Cu GND geodesic from C513.2: 7.61 mm to via 288.4,151.55 and 19.2 mm to pin 19 (21.9 mm to the EP). Nearest GND via to each 22 uF cap GND pad: C511 4.22, C513 6.1, C514 5.0, C515 5.4, C517 5.5, C518 4.4 mm (none within 3 mm). SW (pins 17/18 -> L510.1) is about 2.1 mm of 0.25 mm F.Cu; the 7.28 mm net total includes the BTST branch. PMID: 0.25 mm F.Cu plus 5.49+1.66 mm In2 0.25 mm and 2 vias. CHG_BAT: 4.01+10.42 mm In1 0.25 mm, routed diagonally under U511. KILIM 1110 / 750 ohm = 1.48 A and KICHGSET 3810: 5.62k -> 1.475 A, both verified in the datasheet. SW abs max 13 V, with footnote '(1) The inherent switching noise voltage spikes should not exceed the absolute maximum rating on SW pin. A tight layout minimizes switching noise.'
verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced every geometric claim. The boost hot loop (HS FET -> SYS -> CSYS -> PGND -> LS FET) runs through two 0.2 mm vias and In2. Its HF return then travels 7.6 mm of fragmented F.Cu pour plus In1, or 19 mm of F.Cu, to the single 0.2 mm GND via at pins 19/20. This is a direct deviation from §11.1 priority 1 ('SYS output capacitor as close to SYS and GND pins as possible'). The placement audit marked it PASS at 4.51 mm and deferred items 6/7 to routing. Routing then added no EP or cap GND vias, and the F16 dogbone moved both the SYS and the GND via further out (via_off_pad.md rows 60/61). Rough loop inductance is several nH against about 1-2 nH for a TI-style layout. With about 2 A peak inductor current and ns edges, the overshoot above an 8.4-8.6 V SYS can plausibly approach the 13 V SW limit, so the overstress path is credible but not measured. The impact is narrower than the finding implies. A U511 failure kills only the Mode-2 charger. JP510 is open by default, and even a shorted U511 would put at most about 5 V onto Dir_Chrg_In, so the FC copy is not at risk. The missing EP vias are a real §11.1 item 6 miss, but the thermal consequence is mild: about 0.6-0.7 W loss, TREG 120 C throttles first. The PMID In2 run is in series with the inductor and outside the hot loop, so it costs efficiency and heating (about 32 mOhm), not overshoot. Note that the KiCad stackup lists In2 as 0.035 mm, while JLC04161H-7628 inner layers are 0.5 oz, so the reviewer's 0.5 oz is the fab-correct assumption. Severity stays major: it is a priority-1 manufacturer layout deviation with a plausible device-overstress path, though limited to the bench charger.
verdicts.corrected_description: BQ25886 (U511) SYS output loop violates SLUSD88A §11.1 priority 1. Pins 15/16 reach the only nearby SYS cap, C513 (4.51 mm c-c), through 2 x 0.46/0.20 vias and about 5.7 mm of In2. C514/C518 hang off a 0.25 mm x 3.3 mm F.Cu link. C513.2's GND return is 7.6 mm of F.Cu to the nearest GND via (288.4,151.55) or 19 mm of F.Cu to pins 19/20. U511 has only 2 GND vias within 5 mm, 0 vias in the EP, and no GND via within 3 mm of any 22 uF cap. The added loop inductance raises SW-node overshoot against the 13 V SW abs max (SYS about 8.4-8.6 V), so the risk to U511 is plausible. The consequence is limited to the Mode-2 charger; the FC copy is not exposed (JP510 open by default). Secondary items: no EP thermal vias (thermal impact mild, TREG-protected); SW about 2.1 mm and PMID 7.15 mm In2 at 0.25 mm, CHG_BAT 14.4 mm at 0.25 mm on In1 slicing the GND plane under U511 (resistive/thermal, not hot-loop). Fix: put an HF SYS cap plus C513 at pins 15/16/EP on F.Cu, add GND vias at every cap GND pad and an EP via array, and widen SW/PMID/CHG_BAT.

verdicts.evidence_checked: pcbnew dump of Net-(Q500-D-Pad5): F.Cu 0.25 mm only (11.6 mm incl. pad-to-pad links), vias 196.95,152.939 and 202.227,156.816 (0.46/0.20), In1 0.25 mm 1.40+5.48 = 6.88 mm. No zone on the net. Q500 and Q501 are both rot 0, so the Q500 drains (x=195.075) face the Q501 sources (x=198.825) and the drain node has to jump over Q501. VBAT_BENCH_N load path J500.3 -> Q500 S: In2 1.5/1.0 mm (about 9.3 mm at 1.5 + 9.7 mm at 1.0) -> single via 194.963,161.288 -> F.Cu 1.2/0.8 -> R505.1 -> F.Cu 0.3 mm 1.78+1.44 = 3.22 mm -> single via 191.286,158.546 -> B.Cu 1.0 mm 2.72 mm -> single via 191.436,155.846 -> Q500 pad 3. This is the only path. U500 VSS (pin 6) reaches J500.3 by a separate In1/In2 route that carries no load current, and R502 (V- series) taps B- at via 203.856,148.403 on the main Q501 -> JP607 return path. Schematic notes: PSU window current limit <= 2 A; VDET3 0.200 V, 'about 11 A at 2 x 9 mOhm'. R5460 datasheet: VDET3 tolerance +/-15 mV, tVDET3 8-16 ms, release only when the load is removed. Stackup: In1 0.0152 mm; JLC04161H-7628 inner layers are 0.5 oz.
verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the evidence exactly. Computed copper resistance: common drain about 37 mOhm (31 of it in the In1 neck), VBAT_BENCH_N J500.3 -> Q500 S about 22-32 mOhm (In2 at 1 oz or 0.5 oz), B- from Q501 S to the R502 tap about 6 mOhm. That is about 64-75 mOhm of copper inside the V- to VSS sense loop, against 16-20 mOhm of FET Rds(on). The excess-discharge trip therefore falls to about 2.1-2.5 A nominal (as low as about 1.96 A at VDET3 min 0.185 V), not the ~3.5 A the reviewer estimated and not the ~11 A the sheet note claims. That is right at the bench PSU's 2 A ceiling, and copper TCR at temperature lowers it further. A trip latches DOUT until the load is removed, so a heater or deploy test near the limit would brown out the FC and the replica would misrepresent pack behaviour. Thermally, the 6.9 mm 0.25 mm In1 neck dissipates about 0.125 W (18 mW/mm) at 2 A. IPC-2221 numbers check out (about 0.24 A internal and 0.88 A external at 10 C). Hot copper sits in the bench strip only, so no FC-copy damage. route_report §7 calls sub-1.0 mm BenchPower copper 'L11 stub segments only', which is false here. The fix is cheap: place the FETs drain to drain, use an F.Cu pour, and add multiple vias. Major, with impact understated rather than overstated.
verdicts.corrected_description: Q500/Q501 are placed with the same orientation, so their common drain is routed as 0.25 mm F.Cu plus 6.88 mm of 0.25 mm on In1 (0.5 oz, the GND-plane layer) through two single 0.20 mm vias. VBAT_BENCH_N from J500.3 to the Q500 sources passes three single 0.20 mm vias and 3.2 mm of 0.3 mm F.Cu. All Mode-1 FC current, up to the 2 A PSU limit, flows through this path. Copper in the R5460 V-/VSS sense loop totals about 64-75 mOhm (drain 37, VBAT_BENCH_N 22-32, B- to the R502 tap 6) against about 18 mOhm of FETs. VDET3 (0.200 +/-0.015 V) therefore trips at about 2.0-2.5 A instead of the documented ~11 A, which coincides with the 2 A bench limit and latches DOUT (FC brownout) on high-current tests. The In1 neck also dissipates about 0.13 W at 2 A. Fix: mirror Q501 so the drain rows face each other with an F.Cu pour, take the drain off In1, widen VBAT_BENCH_N, and use at least 2 vias per layer change.

verdicts.evidence_checked: Listed every Dir_Chrg_In track and via (pcbnew dump) and diffed against FC_V5e_Production_Rev2.kicad_pcb. New copper: J500.1 -> In1/In2 1.5 -> JP500.2 -> In2 1.0 -> via 217.581,152.526 -> In2 1.0 (y=158.108) -> via 246.0,157.664 -> B.Cu 1.0 26.1 mm -> via 246.0,131.564 -> In2 7.2 mm -> via 241.1,126.264 -> B.Cu 36.5 mm -> via 243.0,90.464 -> In2 about 31 mm -> via 234.9,65.664 -> F.Cu 1.0/1.2 about 10 mm -> J16.8 (224.5,65.0). JP510.2 joins the same In2 run. All five layer-change vias are single 0.46/0.20. No new track touches J14 pins 1/3/5/7/9. Heritage segments, byte-identical in Rev2: In2 0.635 (224.5,65)-(226.599,66.399)-(226.599,68.399); In2 0.4 mm (226.599,68.399)-(226.599,125.701) 57.3 mm and (222,130.3)-(226.599,125.701) 6.5 mm; via 220.48,130.275 0.8/0.4; B.Cu 0.4 mm about 14.7 mm to J14.1. Netlist Dir_Chrg_In = J14.1/3/5/7/9, J16.8, J500.1, JP500.2, JP510.2, R109.1, R500.1, TP500.1, U16.1. Docs: route_report §2 'Dir_Chrg_In | J16.8 | F.Cu | 1.000 | 3.03 / 14'; brief L11 lists Dir_Chrg_In under the J14 battery attachment (J16 list omits it); attachment_check.py ALLOWED_PADS permits any J16 pin; floorplan_v2.md planned Dir_Chrg_In at J14.1 -> R500.1; route_report_attempt1 reached J14.2 (B-) on F.Cu at 1.0 mm. The battery sheet note says debug_board_v1's 383k ILIM gave 2.9 mA and 'would never charge'.
verdicts.reasoning: The evidence holds. Every bench amp in Mode 1 and Mode 2 enters the FC copy through J16.8. It then runs through the flown board's 0.4 mm inner debug-charge trace to J14.1 and the pours to R109. That changes the behaviour of frozen heritage copper, which falls under the exception the PM allows reviewing. On the flown design this path was never exercised at amps: the debug-board ILIM error noted on the battery sheet meant it charged at about 3 mA. Recomputed with 0.49 mOhm/sq outer and 1.13 (0.5 oz) or 0.49 (1 oz) mOhm/sq inner. New path: about 94-147 mOhm, including 5 single 0.2 mm vias in series against L5's 'two vias per layer change'. Heritage J16.8 -> J14.1: about 103-212 mOhm. Total 0.20-0.36 ohm, so the FC sees 0.4-0.7 V less than J500 at 2 A (0.2-0.36 V at 1 A), and the heritage 0.4 mm trace dissipates 0.4-0.85 W (up to about 13 mW/mm) at 2 A. That is warm (tens of C) but unlikely to damage FR4 or fuse the trace at <= 2 A, so the 'damage' framing is somewhat overstated. Test-validity framing holds: the replica senses at J500 while the FC and INA219 U16 see the dropped voltage. Feasibility of re-attaching at J14 is not proven here, but attempt 1 reached J14.2 on F.Cu and floorplan_v2 planned J14.1, so it is likely reachable within L11. Major is appropriate.
verdicts.corrected_description: The only bench-power path into the FC copy is the Dir_Chrg_In stub at J16.8 (DEBUG). No new copper reaches J14's Dir_Chrg_In pins, even though brief L11 and floorplan_v2 put the battery attachment at J14. From J500.1/JP510.2 the current crosses about 140 mm of new 1.0 mm track with five single 0.46/0.20 vias in series (about 0.09-0.15 ohm). It then runs through the heritage J16.8 -> J14.1 debug-charge link: 0.4 mm In2 for 65 mm plus 0.4 mm B.Cu for 15 mm (about 0.10-0.21 ohm), which never carried amps on the flown board. Total 0.2-0.36 ohm gives a 0.4-0.7 V drop and 0.4-0.85 W in heritage FC-copy copper at the 2 A bench limit (0.2-0.36 V at 1 A). The heating is notable but not destructive, and the FC/INA219 see a lower Dir_Chrg_In than the replica senses at J500. Fix: attach Dir_Chrg_In at J14 odd pins (THT, L11-listed) with a wide stub and paired vias; otherwise document the drop and limit bench current.

verdicts.evidence_checked: FlatSat_V1.kicad_pro netclass_patterns: BenchPower = */VBAT_BENCH_N, VSOLAR_BENCH_A/B, VBUS_CHG, */CHG_SYS, */CHG_BAT, VBUS_EMU, */MID_BENCH. There is no pattern for Net-(Q500-D-Pad5), Net-(D400/D401-A/K), Net-(C511-Pad1), Net-(C512-Pad1) or CHG_DVIN. FlatSat_V1.kicad_dru contains only clearance, annular_width, via_diameter and hole_size rules, with no track_width. route_report §6 itself states that KiCad 10 DRC does not enforce netclass width. Measured widths: CHG_BAT 18.3 mm at 0.25 (14.4 on In1); VBUS_CHG 0.25 mm x 5.7 mm F.Cu from J510 A4/B9 plus 4.2 mm at 0.3; CHG_SYS 0.25 at the pins and a 3.26 mm C514/C518 link; VBAT_BENCH_N 3.2 mm at 0.3; Net-(D400-K) In2 0.25 mm 14.42 mm with 1 via; Net-(D401-K) In2 0.25 mm 16.37 mm; Net-(D400-A)/(D401-A) F.Cu 0.25 mm 6.9/6.1 mm. CHG_DVIN main path Q510 S -> U511.23 is 0.25 mm F.Cu plus In1 0.25 mm 3.4 mm with 2 vias and a 0.1874 mm x 0.54 mm neck; the third via and the other 0.187 mm segments are on the U510 sense branch. Stubs: VBUSP J30.1 0.25-0.3 mm (6.75 mm at 0.3), INHIB_2 0.3 mm x 11.6 mm at x=197.725, B- J15.1 stub through single via 214.831,142.955. layout_report.md line 116 says 'visible in DRC - no width below class' and route_report §7 says the sub-1.0 mm entries are 'all L11 stub segments'; both are contradicted by the charger/replica/injection geometry above. solar_power_injection notes: F400/F401 Ihold 1.85 A at 20 C, Itrip 3.70 A, expected <= 1.2 A; the LT3652 1.0 A charge gives about 0.8-0.9 A input at 12-18 V.
verdicts.reasoning: The facts reproduce. The process gap is real: the auto-named power nodes are unclassed, the named BenchPower nets carry 0.25-0.30 mm segments outside the attachment band, no DRC width rule exists, and the brief §9 exit criterion 'no width below class' is reported as met when it is not. Some details are overstated. CHG_DVIN has 2 vias on its current path, not 3, and its 0.187 mm neck is only 0.54 mm. The SW 0.25 mm run from pin to L510 is about 2.1 mm, not 7.3. The replica sub-claim is in fact understated: I compute a VDET3 trip of about 2.0-2.5 A (see id 12). The highest-impact content duplicates id 12 (replica common drain / VDET3) and overlaps id 11 (PMID/SW/CHG_BAT/CSYS). The residual unique items have modest impact at design currents. Injection K-side 0.25 mm In2 (65-74 mOhm) at the realistic 0.8-1.2 A dissipates about 50-100 mW, a modest rise. Only the PTC fault region (1.85-3.7 A) would badly overheat it, and that copper is bench-strip, not FC copy. VBUS_CHG 0.25 mm x 5.7 mm at 1.48 A is about 11 mOhm / 24 mW. The heritage-band stubs are constrained by frozen copper and already disclosed. The minor severity covers the unique remainder plus the root-cause/process value: adding a track_width DRC rule and classing the auto-named nets is what prevents ids 11/12 from recurring. If the orchestrator merges 11/12 into this as an umbrella, the umbrella severity is major.
verdicts.corrected_description: Root cause behind ids 11 and 12, plus a few residual narrow bench power paths. The L5 netclass widths are not DRC-enforced (no track_width rule in .kicad_dru; KiCad 10 treats netclass width as a routing default only). The auto-named current nodes (Q500/Q501 common drain, D400/D401 A/K, BQ25886 PMID/SW, CHG_DVIN) match no BenchPower pattern. Named BenchPower nets still carry 0.25-0.30 mm segments outside the attachment band (CHG_BAT 18.3 mm incl. 14.4 mm on In1, VBUS_CHG 5.7 mm at 0.25 from J510, VBAT_BENCH_N 3.2 mm at 0.3), contrary to layout_report/route_report claims and the brief §9 'no width below class' gate. Unique residual risks: the VSOLAR injection D400/D401 cathode runs are 0.25 mm on 0.5 oz In2 for 14-16 mm, fine at the 0.8-1.2 A expected but unprotected by the PTC (1.85 A hold / 3.7 A trip) in a fault; VBUS_CHG/CHG_DVIN necks are small resistive losses. Replica (VDET3 about 2.0-2.5 A) is covered by id 12 and the charger loop/widths by id 11. Fix: add track_width (min 1.0 mm) DRC rules for BenchPower/FCPower outside the attachment pads, label and class the auto-named power nodes, and re-route; injection and VBUS_CHG are next-rev on their own.

result.summary: 13 items from 16 kept findings after merging duplicates (3+17, 7+12, 8+16, 10+13) and settling the L200 polarity dispute against the datasheet's own field/loop model. Five are fix-this-rev: all sit in the new bench strip or the owner-ruled attachment framework, none touches frozen FC copper. (1) Mode 2 feeds the FC from BQ25886 BAT instead of SYS and cannot hold the FC up: deterministic, 8 mm of routing to fix. (2) Every bench amp enters the FC copy through J16.8 and the heritage 0.4 mm debug-charge trace (0.2-0.36 ohm): attach at J14 as brief L11 intended. (3) The R5460 replica's V-/VSS sense loop contains 64-75 mOhm of 0.25 mm copper, so excess-discharge trips at 2.0-2.5 A, on top of the 2 A bench limit, instead of ~11 A. (4) The U200 VREG cell is not the reference/flown cell (LX on In2 through a POFV via, three GND islands, COUT return under the inductor); the L200 polarity is in fact mirror-consistent and the proposed rotate-and-swap would make it wrong, so the remedy is to copy the flown U18/L3 cell verbatim. (5) BQ25886 SYS hot loop runs through two 0.2 mm vias and 7.6-19 mm of GND return with no EP or cap vias; do it in the same pass as (1). The rest are next-rev or procedure items. One packet side note is promoted to a trivial text fix: lower the VSOLAR bench hard maximum from 24 V to 18 V because heritage C40 is a 10 V part. QSPI length closes with no action at <=75 MHz.

items.title: Mode 2 (USB charger) feeds the FC from BQ25886 BAT, not SYS: charge termination, recharge deglitch and safety timer cut FC power
items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: U511.13/14 BAT (CHG_BAT) -> JP510.1 (257.3,145.79) -> JP510.2 Dir_Chrg_In. CHG_SYS = U511.15/16 + C513/C514/C517/C518 + TP511 (265.5,144.8), no load. R515 5.62k -> ICHG 1.475 A, ITERM/IPRECHG ~147 mA.
items.rationale: Merged ids 3 and 17 (both confirmed, verifier raised 17 to major). D11 forbids a pack in Mode 2, so BAT is the FC's only source and the charger treats FC current as charge current. FC load under ITERM (likely at idle: 100 mA on 3.3 V reflects to 50-80 mA at 8.4 V) -> termination after 250 ms, BATFET off (SLUSD88A 8.3.7.3), the 130-240 uF of FC input capacitance collapses in ms, recharge waits 250 ms -> brownout/reboot loop. FC load above ITERM -> no termination, 12 h safety timer (24 h in DPM) suspends BAT. Start-up is also limited to 100 mA below 4.4 V and 147 mA below 6.0 V. SYS is the datasheet's no-battery 'instant-on' output (8.3.6.1: regulated >= 6.2 V with no battery, VBAT+50 mV after termination, so ~8.25-8.45 V tracking the BAT cap). Deterministic physics, one of three documented bench modes fails, no damage path, Mode 1 unaffected, debug_board_v1 is not heritage (never assembled).
items.action: Schematic: move JP510 pin 1 from CHG_BAT to CHG_SYS; leave CHG_BAT with C515 and TP512 only. PCB: delete the CHG_BAT In1 0.25 mm run (272.25,146.13)->JP510.1; route JP510.1 from TP511 (265.5,144.8) on F.Cu at 1.0 mm (~8.4 mm; BenchPower pattern */CHG_SYS already applies). The existing TP511 -> SYS-pin path (F.Cu 1.0-1.5 mm, In2 1.0 mm 7.7 mm, via 279.66,152.2) is adequate for the <=0.75 A the 1.48 A input limit can deliver at 8.4 V. Keep the rule 'JP510 never with J500 PSU'. Rewrite the Mode 2 sheet note: FC fed from SYS, STAT no-battery blink still expected on the BAT side. If boards are ordered first: JP510 open, wire TP511 -> TP500 (190.0,163.5).
items.verification: Bench Mode 2 (USB only, no pack, JP510 fitted): log Dir_Chrg_In with the FC idle for 30 min and under a 0.5 A load step; pass = no dropouts, voltage 8.2-8.5 V. items.title: U200 core-regulator cell is not the mandated reference/flown layout; L200 polarity is mirror-consistent as built and the proposed rotate-and-swap would make it wrong
items.location: emulator_mcu: U200 (273.145,94.855) pins 47-50 at y=91.418; L200 (279.4,90.75) rot 0, pad 1 (dot, 278.7) = EMU_VREG_LX, pad 2 (280.1) = 1V1_EMU; C217 COUT (278.8,92.4) rot 180, GND west / 1V1 east; C213 CIN (276.62,90.15); C215 CFILT (278.8,93.91). EMU_VREG_LX: pin 48 -> F.Cu 0.127 mm -> via (275.145,90.55) -> In2 0.25 mm 3.1 mm inside the 3V3_EMU pour -> POFV via (278.403,90.408) in L200.1. COUT GND return: 0.127 mm x 3.4 mm under the L200 body to via (279.66,89.575). R703/R704 (22 ohm USB series) at (272.845,89.1)/(274.645,89.1) occupy the space north of the pins.
items.rationale: Merged ids 10 and 13 with the refuted L200 entry. Polarity resolved against RP2350 DS 6.3.8.3 and Fig. 28: the coupling that matters is the inductor's leakage field into 'the loop formed by VREG_LX through the inductor and COUT', and Fig. 28 shows a flat racetrack winding with a vertical core field whose direction follows current direction (non-dot -> dot = drawn direction). Reference L1/C7 and flown L3/C66 are the same handedness (L3 is the reference cell rotated 45 deg): dot/1V1 on the left facing the inductor from the chip, LX and COUT-GND on the right, L-COUT loop counter-clockwise, field +z. FlatSat L200/C217 is the left-right mirror of that pair (LX west/1V1 east; COUT GND west/1V1 east), the loop circulates clockwise, and with the same-chirality part current flows dot -> non-dot, so the field is -z: same coupling sign as the reference. Rotating 180 deg and swapping the nets (id 10's remedy) would restore +z over a clockwise loop, i.e. the 'wrong way round' case. So the as-built polarity is defensible; the defect is that the cell is not the reference at all (DS 6.3.8: 'must be strictly followed'; 6.3.8.1: F.Cu-only LX, single-point GND with two adjacent vias, CFILT on its own via, no copper under the inductor, COUT between VREG_VIN and VREG_PGND): LX goes through two vias and In2 into a via-in-pad, CIN/COUT/PGND are three separate F.Cu GND islands joined only through In1, the COUT return runs under the inductor body, C215 shares COUT's GND via, VREG_AVDD runs 1.25 mm from LX on In2. The placement doc (placement_emulator_core.md N-1/N-2) required these and routing dropped them. Risk is 1V1_EMU regulation/noise at load transients on the emulator that every bench test depends on, not damage; RPi says other layouts 'could work' at the designer's own risk. A proven cell (flown U18) exists, the fix is local and pre-order, and it removes one of the 7 POFV vias (L200.1).
items.action: Copy the flown U18/L3/C65/C66/C67 regulator cell verbatim, same handedness and pin mapping (pad 1 dot = 1V1, pad 2 = LX), placed north of pins 47-50 as in the reference (CIN ~1.2 mm, COUT ~2.1 mm, L ~3.75 mm from the pins, centred on pin 48 x=275.145): move R703/R704 and C212 ~2 mm west to clear y 87-91. LX on F.Cu only, no via; one F.Cu GND island for CIN/COUT/PGND with 2 adjacent vias to the EP; C215 on its own GND via; cut In2 copper under LX; VREG_AVDD away from LX. Fallback if the cell cannot move: re-route in place keeping the as-built dot-on-LX orientation, tie the three GND islands on F.Cu, take the COUT return out from under L200, give C215 its own via, and move LX onto F.Cu. In no case apply the rotate-and-swap alone.

items.rationale: id 11, confirmed. Boost hot loop (HS FET -> SYS -> CSYS -> PGND -> LS FET) carries ~2 A peaks with ns edges through several nH of extra loop inductance, so SW overshoot above the 8.4-8.6 V SYS can plausibly approach the 13 V SW absolute maximum (SLUSD88A 7.1 footnote: spikes must not exceed SW abs max, tight layout minimises them). Consequence is the Mode 2 charger only: JP510 is open by default and a failed U511 cannot put more than ~5 V on Dir_Chrg_In, so the FC copy is not exposed. EP thermal vias are a real item-6 miss but mild (0.6-0.7 W, TREG 120 C throttles). PMID In2 run is outside the hot loop (efficiency/heating only). After item 1, SYS also feeds the FC, so CSYS quality matters more, and CHG_BAT carries no load so its In1 run becomes a don't-care. Item 1 reopens this exact area, so the incremental cost is modest.

Against RP2350 DS 6.3.8.3 and Fig. 28 (vertical core field, coupling into the LX-L-COUT loop), the FlatSat L200/C217 pair is the left-right mirror of the reference pair with the same-chirality part, so dot-on-LX reverses the field to match the mirrored loop; the swap would produce the wrong-way-round case. The underlying defect (non-reference cell) is carried as item 4 with 'copy the flown cell verbatim' as the remedy. The refuted L200 entry's physics is adopted; it is not a separate item.

Refuted 'DRV2605L U303 VDD has no 1 uF': dropped. Face 0 is a golden copy of the flight face (XY_Faces_V3r has the same 100 nF on VDD, 1 uF on REG), DS 9.2.2.2 itself recommends 0.1 uF, and ripple impact is ~19 mV. At most a datasheet-parity note for the XY_Face design, not FlatSat V1.

id 15 'sustained heating damages FC-copy copper' framing: softened in item 2. 0.4-0.85 W over 65 mm of inner trace is tens of degrees, not destructive; the fidelity and heritage-behaviour-change points carry the item.
id 11 EP thermal-via sub-item: kept inside item 5 but weighted as mild (0.6-0.7 W, TREG 120 C throttles first); PMID In2 run reclassified as resistive loss outside the hot loop.

Heritage C40 10 V rating on a >= 11.7 V flight net (id 18 verifier side note): not a FlatSat defect in itself since flight already exceeds the rating; carried only as the 18 V bench-window cap in item 8 and an upstream FC finding to file.

id 16 'CHG_DVIN three vias / SW 7.3 mm' details: corrected per verifier (2 vias on the current path, 0.187 mm neck only 0.54 mm, SW ~2.1 mm); the process gap (no track_width rule, unclassed auto-named nets, false 'no width below class' claims) is what item 6 keeps.
id 13 'In1 GND under LX/L200 not cut' sub-point: not counted (flown L3 has the same, per its verifier); item 4 asks for the In2 cut only where the copied cell needs it.

result.summary: 14 verified findings merged into 13 items (plus one heritage note surfaced by a verifier). Four are fix-this-rev because they make a documented bench mode fail or stress hardware: (1) Mode 2 feeds the FC from BQ25886 BAT instead of SYS, so the FC reboots at charge termination or loses power at safety-timer expiry; (2) replica current-path copper (common drain on 0.25 mm In1 plus VBAT_BENCH_N necks) sits inside the R5460 V-/VSS sense loop and pulls the excess-discharge trip from the documented ~11 A to ~2.0-2.5 A, coincident with the 2 A bench limit; (3) all bench current enters the FC copy through the J16.8 debug stub and the heritage 0.4 mm inner trace (0.2-0.36 ohm, 0.4-0.85 W at 2 A) instead of the J14 attachment the brief specified; (4) BQ25886 SYS hot loop runs through two 0.2 mm vias and In2 with no GND vias at any charger cap or the EP. The L200 polarity item is NOT carried as fix-this-rev: my own geometry check (flown loop CCW with current non-dot to dot; emulator loop CW with current dot to non-dot) plus Raspberry Pi's stated mechanism (leakage field direction set by winding and current flow coupling into C7) support the refuter's mirror argument, so the packet's rotate-and-swap would likely create the wrong-way condition; it becomes monitor-in-test with a trivial bench A/B and a next-rev re-layout copying the flown U18/L3 cell. The rest are next-rev or accepted with this-rev procedure mitigations. Nothing in the packet can damage the FC copy at bench currents of 1 A or less.

items.title: Mode 2 (USB charger) powers the FC from BQ25886 BAT, not SYS: termination/recharge brownout cycling and safety-timer cut-off
items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: U511 pins 13/14 BAT (CHG_BAT) -> JP510.1 -> JP510.2 Dir_Chrg_In; CHG_SYS (U511.15/16, C513/C514/C517/C518, TP511) has no load. PCB: JP510 at (257.3,148.33), U511 at (277.0,152.2), SYS via (279.663,152.2). Packet ids 3 + 17 merged.
items.rationale: Mode 2 never has a pack (rule D11), so BAT, a charge-controlled port, is the FC's only supply. R515 5.62k gives ICHG 1.475 A and ITERM/IPRECHG about 147 mA (120-180 mA over temperature). An idle FC at 8.4 V draws below ITERM, so after the 250 ms tTERM_DGL the BATFET opens (SLUSD88A 8.3.7.3); the ~22 uF on BAT plus FC input caps collapse in milliseconds, well inside the 250 ms recharge deglitch, so the FC browns out and reboots repeatedly (this is the 'expected STAT blinking' with the FC as the victim). A load above ITERM instead hits the 12 h (24 h in DPM) safety timer. Start-up is limited to 100 mA below 4.4 V and 147 mA below 6.0 V. The datasheet's no-battery 'instant-on' output is SYS, regulated at or above VSYS_MIN 6.2 V, which is unloaded here. Both verifiers confirmed; no damage path, Mode 1 unaffected, but one of three documented bench modes cannot keep the FC running.
items.action: Schematic: move JP510 pin 1 from CHG_BAT to CHG_SYS (TP511 is on that net); leave CHG_BAT with C515/TP512 only. PCB: re-route the JP510.1 link from the CHG_SYS copper (C513 column / via 279.663,152.2) at >=1.0 mm BenchPower width instead of from U511.13/14. Rewrite the sheet note so STAT blinking is described as BAT-cap cycling with the FC on SYS. If boards are already ordered: leave JP510 open and fit a 22 AWG wire TP511 (CHG_SYS) -> TP500 (Dir_Chrg_In), keeping the D11 / no-PSU-with-J510 rule.
items.verification: Mode 2 bring-up, no pack, JP500 open: log Dir_Chrg_In at >=1 kS/s with the FC idle (<147 mA at Dir_Chrg_In) for 30 min, then a 13 h soak at >200 mA load. Pass = no excursion below 6.0 V and no FC reset. As built, the idle test shows reboot cycles within seconds of the load falling below ITERM, so the ATP step is diagnostic either way.

items.title: Replica battery current path copper inside the R5460 sense loop lowers the excess-discharge trip from ~11 A to ~2.0-2.5 A, coincident with the 2 A bench limit
items.location: PCB bench strip: Net-(Q500-D-Pad5) Q500 pads 5-8 (195.075,153.5-157.4) -> 0.25 mm F.Cu -> via 0.46/0.20 (196.95,152.94) -> In1 0.25 mm 1.40+5.48 mm -> via (202.23,156.82) -> Q501 pads 5-8; VBAT_BENCH_N J500.3 (213.08,165.2) -> In2 1.5/1.0 mm -> single via (194.963,161.288) -> R505.1 -> F.Cu 0.3 mm 3.22 mm -> via (191.286,158.546) -> B.Cu -> via (191.436,155.846) -> Q500 pads 1-3. Sense: U500.6 VSS on VBAT_BENCH_N via a separate In1 route near J500.3; U500.3 V- via R502 to B-. Packet ids 7 + 12 + replica part of 16 merged.
items.rationale: Reproduced the common-drain geometry myself: Q500.8 -> Q501.5 is 38.9 mOhm (31 mOhm in the 6.9 mm In1 neck at 0.5 oz), Q500.5 -> Q501.8 is 48.9 mOhm. Verifier 12's pcbnew trace adds 22-32 mOhm on the VBAT_BENCH_N load path and ~6 mOhm on B- to the R502 tap, all inside the V- to VSS loop, against 16-20 mOhm of FET Rds(on). VDET3 0.200 +/-0.015 V then corresponds to about 2.0-2.5 A (verifier 7 counted only the drain link and got 3.5 A; the 2.0-2.5 A figure is the complete loop). At the sheet's 2 A PSU limit the sensed drop is 0.17-0.19 V, inside the 0.185-0.215 V trip band, and copper TCR at temperature pushes it higher, so a DOUT latch (FC brownout, released only by removing the load) on a 2 A heater or deploy test is credible. Brief L5 anticipates ~3 A shunt-path currents. The replica then misrepresents battery_pack_v2 behaviour, which is its only purpose. The In1 neck also dissipates ~0.13 W at 2 A. No damage path; the fix is confined to the bench strip.
items.action: Place Q501 mirrored so its pads 5-8 face Q500 pads 5-8 and tie the two drain rows with an F.Cu pour or >=2 mm track (<5 mOhm), no inner-layer segment; put a local label on the net and add it to BenchPower. Widen VBAT_BENCH_N from J500.3 to the Q500 source pads to >=1.0 mm on F/B.Cu with paired 0.8/0.4 vias in place of the three single 0.46/0.20 vias. Correct the sheet's trip-current note to the computed value. If boards are already built: bridge Q500 pads 5-8 to Q501 pads 5-8 with tinned braid over the top and run a wire from J500.3 to the Q500 source pads.
items.verification: 4-wire resistance Q500 pad 8 to Q501 pad 5 <=5 mOhm (as built ~39-49 mOhm). V(J500.3) minus V(R502.2 tap) at 2.0 A DC <=60 mV (as built ~170-190 mV). ATP: 2.0 A load on Dir_Chrg_In for 60 s cold and again after 10 min at 1.5 A: TP503/TP504 gate drive stays high, no DOUT latch.

items.title: All bench current enters the FC copy through the J16.8 DEBUG stub and the heritage 0.4 mm inner debug-charge trace instead of the J14 battery attachment
items.rationale: Verifier confirmed by diffing every Dir_Chrg_In track against Rev2. The new run is 0.09-0.15 ohm with five single 0.2 mm-drill vias in series (brief L5 asks for two 0.8/0.4 vias per layer change); the heritage J16.8 -> J14.1 link adds 0.10-0.21 ohm and never carried more than ~3 mA on the flown board (debug-board ILIM error noted on the sheet). That is thermal stress on the one copper the board is not supposed to touch (tens of degrees rise on a 0.4 mm 0.5 oz inner trace, not destructive) and a permanent fidelity error: the replica senses at J500 while the FC and INA219 U16 see hundreds of mV less, so brown-out and VBATT-telemetry tests do not match a pack on J14. Brief L11 and floorplan_v2 both put Dir_Chrg_In at J14; attempt-1 routing reached J14.2 on F.Cu, so a compliant stub is feasible. Ranked above the charger hot loop because it affects every Mode-1 and Mode-2 test and involves the FC copy.

items.title: BQ25886 SYS hot loop violates layout priority 1: SYS caps reached through two 0.2 mm vias and In2, no GND via at any charger cap, no EP vias; SW/PMID/CHG_BAT at 0.25 mm
items.location: PCB: U511 (277.0,152.2) SYS pins 15/16 (278.962,151.95/152.45) -> 0.25 mm F.Cu -> via 0.46/0.20 (279.663,152.2) -> In2 ~5.7 mm -> via (281.462,154.95) -> C513.1 (280.845,156.55); C513.2 GND return 7.6 mm F.Cu to via (288.4,151.55) or 19 mm to pins 19/20; EP pad 25 (2.7x2.7) 0 vias; nearest GND via to C511/C513/C514/C515/C517/C518 GND pads 4.2-6.1 mm; SW pins 17/18 -> L510.1 0.25 mm ~2.1 mm; PMID L510.2 -> pins 21/22 0.25 mm incl. 7.15 mm In2 and 2 vias; CHG_BAT In1 0.25 mm 4.01+10.42 mm under U511. Packet id 11 + charger parts of 8 and 16 merged.
items.rationale: Verifier rasterised the fills and reproduced every distance. The boost hot loop (HS FET -> SYS -> CSYS -> PGND -> LS FET) runs through two 0.2 mm vias and In2 and returns via fragmented F.Cu pour and In1 to the single GND via near pins 19/20, several nH against 1-2 nH for the TI layout (SLUSD88A 11.1 item 1: SYS output capacitor as close to SYS and GND pins as possible). With ~2 A peak inductor current and ns edges, SW overshoot above an 8.4-8.6 V SYS can plausibly approach the 13 V SW absolute maximum (datasheet footnote: switching spikes must not exceed it, a tight layout minimises them). Consequence is limited to the Mode-2 charger: JP510 is open by default and a shorted U511 puts at most ~5 V onto Dir_Chrg_In, so the FC copy is not at risk. EP vias missing (11.1 item 6) is thermally mild (0.6-0.7 W, TREG 120 C). Real charge current is input-power limited to ~0.8-1.1 A, so the 0.25 mm SW/PMID/CHG_BAT runs are resistive/thermal losses (<0.1 W each), not hot-loop items. Disposed fix-this-rev because the charger block must be re-opened anyway for rank 1 and the overstress path is plausible hardware damage; if the owner takes the bench-wire route for rank 1 instead, this drops to monitor-in-test with the scope gate below.
items.action: Place C513 (22 uF) plus a new 0.1-1 uF 25 V 0402 directly across SYS pins 15/16 and PGND 19/20 on F.Cu (swap positions with C512 BTST if needed). Add GND vias (2x 0.46/0.20 or 1x 0.8/0.4) at every 22 uF GND pad: C510, C511, C513, C514, C515, C517, C518. Add a 3x3 array of 0.3 mm vias in the U511 EP to In1/B.Cu. Route SW (pins 17/18 -> L510.1) and PMID (L510.2 -> pins 21/22) on F.Cu at >=0.8 mm, rotating L510 so pad 2 faces C511. Delete the CHG_BAT 0.25 mm In1 run under U511 and re-route at >=0.6 mm on F.Cu/In2. Fallback without respin: scope SW with a short-ground probe at 5 V / 1.48 A input and 1 A BAT load; if the peak exceeds 11 V, raise R514 to derate ILIM.
