items.title: U200 VREG cell departs from the mandated RP2350 reference: mirrored loop with contested L200 orientation, LX through two vias on In2 into a via-in-pad, CIN/COUT/PGND on separate F.Cu GND islands, CFILT sharing COUT's via
items.location: emulator_mcu.kicad_sch L200 (AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T, L_pol_2016, pad 1 = polarity dot). PCB: U200 (273.145,94.855) pins 47-50 at y=91.418; L200 (279.4,90.75) pad 1 (278.7) = EMU_VREG_LX, pad 2 (280.1) = 1V1_EMU; LX: pin 48 -> F.Cu 0.127 mm 0.87 mm -> via 0.40/0.20 (275.145,90.55) -> In2 0.25 mm 3.1 mm -> via-in-pad (278.403,90.408); C213 CIN (276.62,90.15), C217 COUT (278.8,92.4, rot 180, GND pad west), C215 CFILT (278.8,93.91) tied to C217.2's 3.4 mm 0.127 mm trace under the L200 body; VREG_AVDD In2 ~1.25 mm from LX In2. Flown reference cell: U18 (206.08,85.42, -45), L3 (212.9,81.7) pad 1 = +1V1, pad 2 = VREG_LX, F.Cu only, C65/C66/pin 47 one F.Cu island. Packet ids 10 + 13 and the refuted L200 entry merged.
items.rationale: The packet contains a confirmed 'major, fix this rev: swap L200 pins and rotate 180 degrees' and a refuted entry arguing the opposite. I recomputed the geometry: in the chip frame the flown loop (pin 48 -> L3 LX pad east -> L3 1V1 pad west/dot -> C66 -> pin 47) circulates CCW with current flowing non-dot to dot; the emulator loop (pin 48 -> L200 LX pad west/dot -> 1V1 pad east -> C217 -> pin 47) circulates CW with current flowing dot to non-dot. Raspberry Pi's stated mechanism (hardware-design guide 2.1, as quoted in the EEVblog thread: the leakage field 'radiates in a direction depending on which way the coil is wound' and current flow, and a wrong-way inductor's field 'interferes with the regulator output capacitor (C7)') is a flux-through-loop coupling whose sign is the product of field direction and loop circulation. Both factors are reversed on the emulator, so the as-built orientation is the mirror-consistent one, and the packet's rotate-and-swap would flip exactly one factor and most likely create the wrong-way condition. Neither side can be proven from the documents, so the direction question is settled on the bench, where the symmetric pads make a 180-degree A/B a two-minute rework. Independently of orientation, the cell violates DS 6.3.8.1 ('must be strictly followed') and placement requirements N-1/N-2: LX via In2 with a via-in-pad (flown: F.Cu, 0 vias), three separate GND islands joined only through single vias to In1, COUT return under the inductor, CFILT sharing the high-current GND via. Risk is degraded 1V1_EMU regulation and noise on the emulator MCU, not damage; RPi notes non-reference layouts generally still execute code. The verifier for id 13 confirmed the fills are current (refill produced a byte-identical board).
items.action: Do NOT apply the pin-swap-and-rotate this rev. Bring-up: measure 1V1_EMU at TP202 with a short-ground 500 MHz probe at idle and under a load step (both cores idle -> busy loop at 150 MHz with QSPI XIP reads), and compare with the FC's +1V1 under the same step. If ripple, bursting or overshoot is worse than the FC's, rotate L200 180 degrees (pads symmetric, routing unchanged), re-measure, and record which orientation wins. Next rev: copy the flown U18/L3/C65/C66 cell verbatim (same relative placement and dot side, LX on F.Cu with no vias, CIN/COUT/PGND on one F.Cu island with their own via cluster, C215 on its own via, no return trace under L200, VREG_AVDD routed away from LX) so the orientation question disappears, and run a parity check of the U200 cell against U18 the way heritage.py checks the FC.
items.verification: TP202 1V1_EMU: ripple <50 mVpp idle, no sub-harmonic bursting, load-step excursion <100 mV, and equal to or better than FC +1V1 in the same test; repeat after a 180-degree L200 rotation and keep the better orientation. Next rev: U200 cell geometry diff against U18 shows identical relative placement.

'Likely damage' is overstated: R500 at 1.3-1.8x rating and ~25 mA substrate current give plausible degradation, not certain failure, and polarity silk is already planned (L8). Human-error scenario on the replica only.

items.title: Synthetic midpoint R503/R504 (1.0k 1%) leaves negative worst-case margin to the R5460N208AA over-charge threshold at the stated 8.4 V PSU limit
items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: R503/R504 1.0k 1% 0805 (C17513) -> MID_BENCH -> R501 -> U500.4 VC; sheet note 'PSU 4.9 V <= V <= 8.4 V ... LT3652 float 8.38 V, 120 mV below the over-charge trip'. Packet id 4.
items.rationale: Verifier reproduced: opposite-limit 1% resistors give a 0.505 split, so at 8.40 V one synthetic cell sees 4.242 V against a minimum VDET1 of 4.225 V (25 C) / 4.220 V (-5 to 55 C); worst case COUT trips at 8.366 V, below the FC LT3652 float of 8.378 V. The sheet's 120 mV margin assumes typical VDET1 and a perfect divider. A trip only opens Q501 and leaves the FC fed through its body diode (~0.7 V drop), and same-reel 1% parts usually match to ~0.2%, so this is a low-probability test-validity nuisance, not damage.
items.action: This rev: change the sheet note and bench procedure to a PSU limit of 8.3 V and treat a COUT trip above 8.3 V as a possible divider artifact. Next rev: R503/R504 as 0.1% or a matched pair.
items.verification: Measure V(MID_BENCH) at 8.40 V: both halves within +/-5 mV of 4.20 V; COUT must not trip below 8.35 V.

result.summary: Chair merge of the PCB and QA lists: 12 items from the same 16 verified findings, 9 of them with identical severity/disposition from both principals. Four are fix-this-rev on the PM's own criterion (bench mode fails or hardware is stressed), all confined to the bench strip and the owner-ruled attachment framework, none touching frozen FC-copy copper: (1) Mode 2 feeds the FC from BQ25886 BAT instead of SYS and cannot keep the FC up; (2) all bench battery current enters the FC copy through the J16.8 debug stub and the heritage 0.4 mm inner trace (0.2-0.36 ohm) instead of the J14 attachment the brief specified; (3) the R5460 replica's V-/VSS sense loop contains 64-75 mOhm of 0.25-0.30 mm copper so excess-discharge trips at 2.0-2.5 A, on top of the 2 A bench limit; (4) the BQ25886 SYS hot loop runs through two 0.2 mm vias and In2 with no GND via at any charger cap and no EP vias, done in the same pass as (1). Three disagreements decided: the U200 VREG cell goes monitor-in-test with a next-rev copy of the flown U18/L3 cell (QA position; the PM criterion is failure or damage, neither is shown, the rotate-and-swap is withdrawn by both principals, and reopening the EMU_FANOUT area carries its own regression risk); the BenchPower track_width DRC rule and net labels go in this rev (PCB position; it is the acceptance check for items 2-4 and costs nothing); the VSOLAR bench hard maximum drops from 24 V to 18 V (PCB position; heritage C40 on V_SOLAR_SENSE is a 10 V X5R, the stated nominal window already tops out at 18 V, and the change is text only). Rank 2/3 order follows the PCB principal: the J16.8 path affects every test in every mode and loads heritage copper, the replica trip only manifests at the top of the window. Remaining items are next-rev with this-rev procedure mitigations, one accepted by owner ruling R9, and the QSPI length topic is closed with no action at CLKDIV >= 2. Nothing in the packet can damage the FC copy at bench currents of 1 A or less.

items.title: Mode 2 (USB charger) feeds the FC from BQ25886 BAT, not SYS: charge termination, recharge deglitch and safety timer cut FC power
items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: U511.13/14 BAT (CHG_BAT) -> JP510.1 -> JP510.2 Dir_Chrg_In (JP510 description: 'charger BAT -> Dir_Chrg_In'). CHG_SYS = U511.15/16 + C513/C514/C517/C518 + TP511 (265.5,144.8), no load. R515 5.62k -> ICHG 1.475 A, ITERM/IPRECHG ~147 mA. PCB: JP510 (257.3,148.33), U511 (277.0,152.2), SYS via (279.663,152.2). Packet ids 3 + 17.
items.rationale: Both principals: major, fix-this-rev, same physics. D11 forbids a pack in Mode 2, so BAT, a charge-controlled port, is the FC's only source. FC idle current (100 mA on 3.3 V reflects to 50-80 mA at 8.4 V) is below ITERM, so after the 250 ms tTERM_DGL the BATFET opens (SLUSD88A 8.3.7.3), the BAT/FC input capacitance collapses in ms, the 250 ms recharge deglitch then restarts it: a brownout/reboot loop, with the FC as the victim of the 'expected STAT blink'. Above ITERM the 12 h (24 h in DPM) safety timer suspends BAT. Start-up is limited to 100 mA below 4.4 V and 147 mA below 6.0 V. SYS is the datasheet's no-battery instant-on output (8.3.6.1, regulated >= 6.2 V, VBAT+50 mV after termination), and it is unloaded. Deterministic, one of three documented bench modes fails, no damage path, Mode 1 unaffected, debug_board_v1 is not heritage.
items.action: Schematic: move JP510 pin 1 from CHG_BAT to CHG_SYS; leave CHG_BAT with C515 and TP512 only. PCB: delete the CHG_BAT In1 0.25 mm run (272.25,146.13)->JP510.1; route JP510.1 from the CHG_SYS copper at TP511 (265.5,144.8) on F.Cu at >= 1.0 mm (~8.4 mm, BenchPower). Keep the rule 'JP510 never with J500 PSU'. Rewrite the Mode 2 sheet note: FC fed from SYS, STAT blink is BAT-cap cycling. If boards are ordered first: JP510 open, 22 AWG wire TP511 -> TP500 (190.0,163.5).
items.verification: Mode 2 bring-up (USB only, no pack, JP500 open, JP510 fitted): log Dir_Chrg_In at >= 1 kS/s with the FC idle for 30 min and under a 0.5 A load step; pass = no excursion below 6.0 V, no FC reset, 8.2-8.5 V. Then a > 13 h soak with the FC above 200 mA to clear the safety-timer case. As built, the idle test shows reboot cycling within seconds, so the ATP step is diagnostic either way.

items.title: All bench battery current enters the FC copy through J16.8 DEBUG and the heritage 0.4 mm inner debug-charge trace (0.2-0.36 ohm), not the J14 attachment the brief specified
items.rationale: Both principals: major, fix-this-rev. Ranked 2 (PCB order) over the replica trip because it affects every Mode-1 and Mode-2 test and is the only bench-current path into the FC copy. Brief L11 and floorplan_v2 put the battery attachment at J14; routing took the shortest legal stub to J16.8. The heritage J16.8 -> J14.1 link (0.10-0.21 ohm) never carried amps on the flown board (debug-board ILIM error gave ~3 mA). Total 0.20-0.36 ohm: 0.4-0.7 V drop and 0.4-0.85 W in frozen FC-copy copper at the 2 A bench limit, 0.2-0.36 V at 1 A. Thermal stress is tens of degrees on a 0.4 mm 0.5 oz inner trace, not destructive ('damage' framing softened by both principals), but it changes the behaviour of heritage copper (the PM's stated exception) and is a permanent fidelity error: the replica senses at J500 while the FC and INA219 U16 see hundreds of mV less, so brown-out and VBATT-telemetry tests near the 4.9 V floor do not match a pack on J14. Five single 0.2 mm vias in series also miss brief L5 (two 0.8/0.4 per layer change). Attempt-1 reached J14.2 on F.Cu, so a compliant stub exists.
items.action: Add an L11-compliant Dir_Chrg_In stub to J14 odd pins 1/3/5/7/9 (THT at (207.0,131.2), rot 90, 2.0 mm pitch, any layer) at >= 1.0 mm (1.5 mm preferred) with paired 0.8/0.4 vias at each layer change, landing on two or more of the odd pins; keep the J16.8 stub as a sense-only tap or remove it. Without a respin: DF11-12 mating pigtail from the J14 power pins to J500/JP510, cap sustained bench current at 1 A otherwise, and print the measured 0.2-0.36 ohm drop in the bring-up document.

items.rationale: Both principals: major, fix-this-rev. QA reproduced the drain-link geometry (38.9 / 48.9 mOhm pad-to-pad, 31 mOhm in the In1 neck); the id 12 verifier traced the full loop: drain 37 + VBAT_BENCH_N 22-32 + B- to the R502 tap 6 = 64-75 mOhm against 16-20 mOhm of FET Rds(on). items.title: BQ25886 SYS hot loop violates layout priority 1: CSYS reached through two 0.2 mm vias and In2, GND return 7.6-19 mm, no EP vias, no GND via within 3 mm of any charger cap
items.location: battery_protection_replica / PCB: U511 (277.0,152.2) SYS pins 15/16 (278.96,151.95/152.45) -> 0.25 mm F.Cu -> via 0.46/0.20 (279.663,152.2) -> In2 ~5.7 mm -> via (281.462,154.95) -> C513.1 (280.845,156.55); C513.2 GND -> 7.61 mm F.Cu to via (288.4,151.55) or 19.2 mm to pins 19/20; EP pad 25 (2.7x2.7) 0 vias; nearest GND via to C511/C513/C514/C515/C517/C518 GND pads 4.2-6.1 mm; SW ~2.1 mm 0.25 mm; PMID 0.25 mm F.Cu + 7.15 mm In2 + 2 vias; CHG_BAT In1 0.25 mm 14.4 mm under U511. Packet id 11 + charger parts of 8 and 16.
items.rationale: Both principals: major, fix-this-rev, coupled to item 1. The boost hot loop (HS FET -> SYS -> CSYS -> PGND -> LS FET) carries ~2 A peaks with ns edges through several nH of extra loop inductance against 1-2 nH for the TI layout (SLUSD88A 11.1 item 1), so SW overshoot above an 8.4-8.6 V SYS can plausibly approach the 13 V SW absolute maximum (7.1 footnote). Plausible, not measured: hardware damage to U511 only. JP510 is open by default and a failed U511 cannot put more than ~5 V on Dir_Chrg_In, so the FC copy is not exposed. EP vias (11.1 item 6) are a real but mild miss (0.6-0.7 W, TREG 120 C throttles); the PMID In2 run and 0.25 mm SW/CHG_BAT runs are resistive losses outside the hot loop at the real 0.8-1.1 A charge current. After item 1, SYS also feeds the FC, so CSYS quality matters more, and CHG_BAT carries no load. Item 1 reopens this exact area, so the incremental cost is modest; QA's condition is adopted: if the owner takes the bench-wire route for item 1 instead of a respin, this drops to monitor-in-test with the scope gate below.
items.action: In the same pass as item 1: place C513 (22 uF) plus a 0.1-1 uF 25 V 0402 directly across SYS pins 15/16 and PGND 19/20 on F.Cu (swap with C512 BTST if space is needed); 3x3 array of 0.3 mm vias in the EP to In1/B.Cu; a GND via (2x 0.46/0.20 or 1x 0.8/0.4) at every 22 uF cap GND pad (C510, C511, C513, C514, C515, C517, C518); SW >= 0.8 mm; PMID to L510.2 on F.Cu >= 0.8 mm (rotate L510 so pad 2 faces C511); delete the CHG_BAT In1 run under U511. Fallback without respin: scope SW with a ground-spring probe at 5 V / 1.48 A input and 1 A BAT load; if peaks exceed 11 V, raise R514 to derate ILIM to ~1 A and record it.
items.verification: Design: GND via within 1 mm of every charger cap GND pad, >= 6 vias in the EP, CSYS loop pins-to-cap-to-pins under 5 mm on F.Cu. Bench: SW (pin 17) peak < 11 V at ILIM 1.48 A / VBUS 5.25 V with 1 A load; SYS ripple at C513 < 100 mVpp; U511 case < 60-80 C after 30 min at ILIM. ATP would otherwise see this only as a dead charger, so the scope check is the gate.

COUT GND return 0.127 mm x 3.4 mm under the L200 body to via (279.66,89.575). VREG_AVDD In2 ~1.25 mm from LX. R703/R704 at (272.845,89.1)/(274.645,89.1) north of the pins. Flown reference: U18 (206.08,85.42,-45), L3 (212.9,81.7) pad 1 = +1V1, pad 2 = VREG_LX, F.Cu only, one GND island. Packet ids 10 + 13 + refuted L200 entry.
items.rationale: Both principals agree on the facts and both withdraw the rotate-and-swap: against RP2350 DS 6.3.8.3 / Fig. 28 and Raspberry Pi's stated mechanism (leakage-field direction set by winding and current flow coupling into the LX-L-COUT loop), the FlatSat L200/C217 pair is the left-right mirror of the reference pair with the same-chirality part (flown loop CCW, current non-dot -> dot; emulator loop CW, current dot -> non-dot), so the as-built dot-on-LX orientation has the same coupling sign and the swap would most likely create the wrong-way case. Disposition disagreement decided for QA (monitor-in-test, next-rev re-layout) over PCB (fix-this-rev, copy the flown cell now): the PM's criterion for fix-this-rev is bench failure or hardware damage; the exposure here is degraded 1V1_EMU regulation/noise under load transients, which RPi says non-reference layouts generally survive ('could work', designer's risk), and no measurement shows failure. The PCB remedy moves R703/R704/C212 and re-routes inside the EMU_FANOUT rule area closed under owner rulings F13/F16, a medium rework in the densest region of the board with its own regression risk, while the symmetric L200 pads make the only contested physics a two-minute bench A/B. Severity stays major because, if it manifests, every bench test depends on the emulator. The id 13 verifier confirmed the fills are current.
items.action: Do NOT apply the pin-swap-and-rotate this rev. Bring-up gate: measure 1V1_EMU at TP202 (280.0,114.5) with a short-ground 500 MHz probe at idle and under a 0 -> 150 mA core load step (both cores idle -> SDK busy loop at 150 MHz with QSPI XIP reads), compared with the FC copy's +1V1 under the same step. If ripple, sub-harmonic bursting or overshoot is worse than the FC's, rotate L200 180 deg (pads symmetric, routing unchanged), re-measure, keep the better orientation and record it. Next rev: copy the flown U18/L3/C65/C66/C67 cell verbatim (same handedness and pin mapping: pad 1 dot = 1V1, pad 2 = LX; CIN ~1.2 mm, COUT ~2.1 mm, L ~3.75 mm from the pins, centred on pin 48; LX on F.Cu with no via; one F.Cu GND island for CIN/COUT/PGND with 2 adjacent vias; C215 on its own via; no copper under L; VREG_AVDD away from LX), moving R703/R704/C212 ~2 mm west; this removes one of the 7 POFV vias (L200.1). Add a U200-cell-vs-U18 parity check to heritage.py. Optional: if the owner reopens routing broadly for items 1-4, the copy may ride that pass at the owner's call.

items.title: VSOLAR injection has no on-board over-voltage element ahead of FC-copy INA219 U8 (accepted per owner ruling R9); lower the bench hard maximum from 24 V to 18 V because heritage C40 (LT3652 VIN bypass) is a 10 V X5R
items.location: solar_power_injection.kicad_sch: J400/J401 -> F400/F401 (2920L 1.85 A PTC) -> D400/D401 Schottky -> JP400/JP401 -> VSOLAR -> U8.1 IN+, R108 2 mOhm -> IC6 LT3652 VIN; sheet note 'Bench PSU setting: 12 V to 18 V nominal, HARD MAXIMUM 24 V (brief section 6.3; F400/F401 are 33 V Vmax ...)'. Heritage C40 10uF +-20% 10V X5R 0603 (Rev2 BOM C19702) on /Power Systems/V_SOLAR_SENSE (C40.1, IC6.1 VIN, IC6.3, R108.2, R65.1, U8.2), PCB (210.4,114.3) B.Cu. Silk reads only 'VSOLAR A' (253.05,152.43) / 'VSOLAR B' (226.2,162.82). Packet id 18 + its verifier's C40 side note.
items.rationale: Merges PCB items 8 and 10 and QA items 7 and 13. Both principals accept the absence of a TVS (R9: PSU OVP is primary; a 20-22 V standoff TVS conducts near 22-27 V and overheats against a current-limited supply; an OV cut-off switch is the right next-rev part) and note that above ~26.5 V nothing on the board protects U8 (26 V abs max) on frozen FC copper. The ceiling disagreement is decided for PCB (18 V) over QA (24 V OVP, 22 V recommended): the chair confirmed C40 is 10 V-rated on the LT3652 VIN node; the flight charger already needs VIN >= VFLOAT + 3.3 V = 11.7 V, so C40 is a heritage FC derating finding in itself, but FlatSat is what grants permission to 24 V, 2.4x rating and at the MLCC dielectric-withstand test level, where a shorted C40 would dump PSU/PTC current (1.85 A hold, 3.7 A trip) into FC-copy copper, the one outcome the board must avoid. The stated nominal window already tops out at 18 V, so nothing is lost, and the change is text only. Minor because the PSU setting is under operator control and the INA219 margin becomes 8 V.

items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: R503/R504 1.0k 1% 0805 (C17513) -> MID_BENCH -> R501 330 -> U500.4 VC; sheet note 'BENCH PSU WINDOW 4.9 V <= V <= 8.4 V' and 'LT3652 float 8.38 V, 120 mV below the over-charge trip'. Packet id 4.
items.rationale: Both principals: minor, next-rev. Opposite-limit 1% resistors give a 0.505 split, so at 8.40 V one synthetic cell sees 4.242 V against a minimum VDET1 of 4.225 V (EA-165: 4.250 +/- 0.025 V at 25 C, 4.220 V over -5 to 55 C); worst-case COUT trip at 8.366 V, below the 8.378 V LT3652 float. Same-reel parts usually match to ~0.2 % (cell 4.208 V, no trip), and a trip only blocks charge and feeds the FC through the Q501 body diode (~0.7 V drop): a low-probability test-validity nuisance, no damage.

items.title: EMU QSPI U200-U201 (30-49 mm, 3-8 vias) is acceptable at the pico-sdk default 75 MHz flash clock: known review topic closed
items.location: emulator_mcu: U200 pins 55-60 to U201 (285.965,95.135); pin-to-pin SCLK 30.4 mm/4 vias, SD0 49.4/3, SD1 46.7/8, SD2 47.2/8, SD3 32.7/5, QSPI_SS 23.4/4; mostly B.Cu (referenced to the In2 3V3_EMU pour) and In2 (referenced to the B.Cu GND pour). Flown U18-U11: 8.5-13.3 mm, 0-2 vias. Packet id 14.
items.rationale: Both principals: info, no-action. Round-trip SCLK + data adds ~0.55 ns against a 6.7 ns half period at 75 MHz (PICO_FLASH_SPI_CLKDIV 2 at 150 MHz); 49 mm is ~65 % of the ~75 mm critical length for 1 ns edges, so the margin is adequate rather than generous and no termination or retiming is needed. Reference planes alternate between GND and 3V3_EMU across layer changes, tolerable at this clock with the nearby decoupling. The 75 MHz figure is an SDK default plus a drc_triage statement, not repo firmware, so the assumption must be pinned.
items.action: None this rev. Pin PICO_FLASH_SPI_CLKDIV >= 2 in the EMU firmware build and note it in the bench procedure; if the flash clock is ever raised (CLKDIV 1 or overclock), run a QMI RXDELAY sweep on hardware before relying on it.
